Yes Madam Expands Beauty Services as Revenue and NTV Rise in Q2 FY27

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Yes Madam Expands Beauty Services as Revenue and NTV Rise in Q2 FY27](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-17T181424.715.jpg)

Yes Madam, an Indian at-home beauty and wellness platform, has reported a 3.9-fold increase in revenue and a 3.5-fold rise in Net Transaction Value (NTV) between Q2 FY25 and Q2 FY27. **The company has achieved an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 402 crore and an annualised NTV run rate of ₹836 crore, reflecting its expanding operations and growing consumer demand.**

In Q2 FY27, the company's revenue rose 11 percent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 79.4 crore from Rs 71.7 crore in Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026). Its NTV grew 12 percent during the same period, increasing from Rs 148.1 crore to Rs 165.8 crore. **Compared with Q2 FY26, revenue and NTV registered year-on-year growth of 69 percent and 75 percent, respectively.**

Founded in 2016 by Mayank Arya, Aditya Arya and Akanksha Vishnoi, Yes Madam operated without external funding for nearly a decade before securing its first institutional investment of ₹50 crore from Info Edge Growth earlier this year. **The company has focused on building a profitable, capital-efficient business while expanding its service network.**

**Yes Madam now operates across more than 55 cities, supported by a network of over 10,000 service professionals.** It fulfils over 3.5 lakh bookings monthly, catering to consumers seeking convenient at-home salon, beauty and wellness services.

**The company's growth strategy has included initiatives focused on hygiene, pricing transparency and service innovation.** It introduced single-use mono-dose kits and separated product and service costs to provide customers with greater clarity on pricing. Its portfolio has also expanded to include premium Korean-inspired beauty services, alongside on-demand salon and spa offerings.

> **Aditya Arya, Co-founder and CEO, Yes Madam said**, "For nearly a decade, we built Yes Madam without external funding by focusing on serving our customers, supporting our service partners and growing the business one step at a time. Built on customer trust, we gradually expanded from one city to another and from a handful of bookings to thousands, creating a business that could stand on its own feet. Our performance in Q2 FY27 reflects how far we have come and the foundation we have built over the years. As we enter our next phase of growth, our ambition is to offer a comprehensive range of beauty and wellness services and make Yes Madam the first name that comes to mind whenever consumers think of beauty services."

**Going forward, the company plans to expand its service portfolio, strengthen its professional network, invest in technology, and increase its presence in existing markets to reach more customers.**

![Metro Brands Q2 Revenue Rises 12.2 Pc to Rs 730 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/dkkerijjtntg.jpg)

Metro Brands reported a 12.2 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 730 crore in the second quarter of FY27, supported by growth across its footwear retail business. ***Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 15.8 percent to Rs 198 crore during the quarter.***

***The company's profit after tax (PAT) rose 12 percent year-on-year to Rs 77 crore, while its EBITDA margin stood at 27.1 percent and PAT margin reached 10.6 percent.*** Gross margin expansion supported profitability, although employee costs increased following minimum wage revisions. Metro Brands also continued investing in talent and brand-building during the quarter.

The company said the shift in the festive calendar affected consumer demand during the quarter, with a larger share of festive-season sales expected to move into the third quarter of FY27. ***Metro Brands continued to grow its online and omnichannel business, with e-commerce sales, including omnichannel transactions, increasing 12 percent year-on-year.*** These channels contributed 14.2 percent of the company's revenue during the quarter.

***The footwear retailer opened 21 stores and closed nine during the quarter. As of September 30, 2026, its retail network comprised 1,053 stores across 223 cities in 31 states and Union Territories.*** Metro Brands operates a portfolio that includes Metro Shoes, Mochi, Walkway, MetroActiv, Da Vinchi and J. Fontini, alongside international footwear brands such as Crocs, Clarks, Skechers and Puma. Its product range also includes accessories such as handbags, belts and wallets.

The company's Q2 FY27 performance reflects continued revenue and earnings growth, alongside ongoing store network expansion and a growing contribution from digital sales. With a larger share of festive demand expected in the next quarter, the company will enter the upcoming period with a focus on retail operations, brand development, and omnichannel sales.

Thermocool Expands Home Appliances Manufacturing in India

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Thermocool Expands Home Appliances Manufacturing in India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/jjnvnnhd.jpg)

Thermocool Home Appliances Ltd plans to invest approximately Rs 40 crore in a new manufacturing facility in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, to increase production capacity and strengthen its in-house manufacturing operations. ***The proposed facility will manufacture air coolers, fans, and small appliances as the company expands its presence in India's home appliances market.***

The facility will cover approximately two acres, with a built-up area of around 40,000 to 60,000 sq ft. ***Its planned annual production capacity will be around 3 to 4 lakh air coolers, 3 to 5 lakh fans and 1 to 2 lakh small appliances.*** The investment is aimed at increasing manufacturing capacity, improving backward integration and giving the company greater control over production, product quality and supply chain operations. The expansion is also expected to support Thermocool's efforts to meet consumer demand across key markets.

> Tushar Gupta, Director of Operations, Thermocool Home Appliances Ltd said, “***The proposed manufacturing facility is an important step in strengthening our production capabilities and supporting our long-term growth plans. We are focusing on greater backward integration and building a manufacturing ecosystem that allows us to respond more efficiently to changing consumer demand. The facility will also support our efforts to expand our product portfolio and strengthen our presence across key markets.***”

***Thermocool currently operates a 25,000 sq ft manufacturing plant in Ghaziabad and is working to increase its production capabilities.*** The company currently manufactures approximately 2,000 to 3,000 air coolers per day and plans to increase daily output by around 25 percent to 35 percent. The planned expansion will incorporate semi-automation, AI-based quality control, and sustainable manufacturing practices. These measures are intended to improve production efficiency and quality management as the company scales its operations.

Thermocool has more than 200 stock-keeping units (SKUs) across large and small appliance categories, with air coolers remaining a key product segment. ***The company has also achieved around 90 percent backward integration in air-cooler manufacturing, enabling it to exercise greater control over the production process.***

> Tanuj Gupta, Director of Sales, Thermocool Home Appliances Ltd said, “***The home appliances market is evolving rapidly, with consumers looking for products that offer performance, value and reliability. Our manufacturing expansion will help us respond to these changing requirements while strengthening our distribution and market presence. We are also exploring opportunities in new categories as we continue to expand our portfolio.***”

Alongside its manufacturing expansion, Thermocool is working to increase its distribution reach across India. ***The company currently has more than 300 distributors and a presence in approximately 5,000 retail stores.*** It is also expanding its visibility across e-commerce and digital commerce platforms.

The company is evaluating opportunities to enter the air-conditioner segment and is exploring other categories, including washing machines, refrigerators and televisions. ***The proposed Ghaziabad facility is expected to support its broader product expansion plans and strengthen its domestic manufacturing capabilities.*** The investment comes as Thermocool looks to increase production, develop its distribution network and expand its presence across India's home appliances market. The proposed facility will add to its existing manufacturing operations and support its plans to enter new product categories.

![Zepto Expands Brand Collabs With Exclusive ITC Collectible](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/dekfjvnedk.jpg)

Zepto has partnered with ITC to introduce Dazzle Vibe Matches: LIT Parivar Edition, a limited-edition matchbox collection inspired by Indian family dynamics and Diwali celebrations. The collection will be available on Zepto across select markets from October 21, 2026. ***The collaboration brings a collectible format to an everyday household product, drawing on the traditional appeal of matchbox designs.***

***The collection features themes centred on family relationships, festive gatherings and the interactions that shape Diwali celebrations.*** The initiative also marks Zepto's first exclusive collectible developed in collaboration with a brand. Through the limited-edition release, the quick commerce platform is exploring a new format for brand collaborations, combining festive products with the appeal of collecting distinctive designs.

> Chandan Mendiratta, Chief Brand Officer, Zepto said, “***Dazzle Vibe Matches: LIT Parivar Edition marks Zepto’s first foray into collectibles through a special collaboration with ITC. We’re bringing back the nostalgia of matchbox collecting with a limited-edition design inspired by the fun, drama, and togetherness of the festive season. This is the first of many unique drops that are planned for our users, with more exciting collaborations to look forward to on Zepto. We thank ITC and our sellers for enabling this.***”

> Rohit Dogra, Chief Executive, Matches and Agarbatti Business Division, ITC Ltd added, “***Through our collaboration with Zepto, we’re bringing a fresh perspective to the nostalgia of matchbox collecting with Dazzle Vibe Matches: LIT Parivar Edition. Inspired by the vibrant dynamics of Indian families and the spirit of Diwali, this limited-edition collection reimagines a familiar everyday object as a collectible. It’s a special way to celebrate the little things that bring people together while introducing a new generation to the charm of collecting.***”

The collection will be available on Zepto from October 21, 2026, in select markets. ***The company plans to introduce more collectible releases through future collaborations, giving users access to additional limited-edition products on its platform.***

The partnership highlights how quick commerce platforms and consumer goods companies are exploring new product formats and brand collaborations during major shopping occasions such as Diwali. For Zepto, the initiative also creates an opportunity to introduce exclusive products alongside its regular assortment of household essentials and festive merchandise.

# TagZ Foods Unveils Consumer Stock Option Plan (CSOP) to Raise Funds

[Retail & Business](/business-investment)

TagZ Foods Unveils Consumer Stock Option Plan (CSOP) to Raise Funds

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
  Sub Editor  Feb 03, 2022 Feb 03, 2022 / ![IndianRetailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/brandlicense/themes/custom/menshealth/images/vicon.webp)
/ 3 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![TagZ Foods Unveils Consumer Stock Option Plan (CSOP) to Raise Funds](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2022-02/TagZ%20image.jpg.jpg "TagZ Foods Unveils Consumer Stock Option Plan (CSOP) to Raise Funds")

TagZ Foods, a Bengaluru-based snacking brand, has launched its Consumer Stock Option Plan (CSOP) where consumers can invest in the company.

The TagZ Foods CSOP has been launched on Tyke, a fintech platform that enables startups to transact and complete their fundraising digitally and instantly. The CSOP has already been oversubscribed 156 percent in two days with nearly a thousand consumers have invested in the firm

Anish Basu Roy, Co-founder of TagZ said, "We have always believed in co-creating our brand alongside our consumers and this is one more step in that direction. TagZ is one of the first consumer brands to enable consumers to invest at such an early stage in the business and partner in the growth journey."

Prior to TagZ, Roy has worked with brands like Nokia and Coca Cola in various sales and [**marketing**](https://www.indianretailer.com/article/technology/digital-trends/7-performance-marketing-skills-to-acquire-in-2022.a7707/) leadership positions across Asia. The TagZ CSOP is currently live on Tyke and consumers can invest as low as Rs 5,000 to participate in the growth of the brand.

Recently, TagZ Foods closed an investment on [**Shark Tank India**](https://www.indianretailer.com/news/shark-tank-india-infuses-rs-5-mn-in-a-skincare-start-up-cosiq.n12420/) and has seen a major spike in sales since then. Last April, TagZ raised $500k in pre-Series A funding from Dexter Angels, Agility Ventures, Venture Catalysts, Dharamveer Chouhan (co-founder, Zostel), Dhruv Toshniwal (co-founder, The Pant Project), and Arjun Vaidya (co-founder, Dr Vaidya's), among others

The company plans to use the funds to expand its product line, production capacity and strengthen its distribution to other cities in the country. Founded by Roy and Sagar Bhalotia in 2019, TagZ Foods is India's first firm to manufacture popped potato chips with 50 percent less fat, international gourmet dips, and a range of premium bar snacks. The startup utilizes technology to make potato chips that claim to have no cholesterol, trans fat, artificial colors, or preservatives.

Packaged salty snacks and biscuits are an over Rs 65,000 crore market, and two of the largest categories within India's fast-moving consumer goods basket. The company said it has been registering a 30 times increase in volume growth and focuses on the top 30-40 million households of the country through an omnichannel strategy that includes more than 30 online partners and over 2,000 offline stores.

Tilaknagar Industries Limited (TI) reported net revenue of Rs 2,059 crore in the first half of FY27, marking a 180 percent year-on-year (YoY) increase, as the company continued to integrate Imperial Blue Whisky into its operations. The company's second-quarter performance also saw Imperial Blue gain over 100 basis points in all-India market share.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, TI recorded net revenue of Rs 1,033 crore, up 172 percent YoY, after adjusting for subsidy. Sales volume reached 8.9 million cases, representing 160 percent growth compared with the same period last year.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) stood at Rs 146 crore, up 143 percent YoY, with a margin of 14.1 percent. Profit after tax, excluding exceptional items and amortization related to the Imperial Blue acquisition, increased 26 percent to Rs 66 crore.

The company said that the states that transitioned from the Transition Services and Manufacturing Agreement (TSMA) following the first quarter had stabilised under its operations. The final remaining state is expected to transition by the end of FY27, which could further support the integration process.

While primary volumes remained largely flat during the quarter, secondary volumes grew 7.8 percent sequentially. Imperial Blue Whisky recorded 8.5 percent quarter-on-quarter growth, while Mansion House Brandy reported a 7.1 percent increase.

Imperial Blue gained market share across 17 states, with Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Assam and Rajasthan among the key contributors. Mansion House Brandy also became the leading brandy across price points in Karnataka in September 2026, according to the company.

> **Amit Dahanukar, Chairman and Managing Director of Tilaknagar Industries**, said the operational transition had progressed and the company's brands continued to expand their reach.

> "With the states transitioned out of TSMA after Q1 now stabilised, we have taken another decisive step towards completing the Imperial Blue integration. Our secondary volumes grew by 7.8 percent during the quarter, and Imperial Blue continued to gain market share across the country, reflecting the strength of our brands and the reach of our expanded distribution network," Dahanukar said.

However, the company continued to face cost pressures from packaging materials, particularly glass. Prices of extra neutral alcohol (ENA), a key input for spirits production, also began rising towards the end of the quarter due to higher fuel and grain costs.

TI said its EBITDA margin would have been approx 16.5 percent without the impact of inflationary pressures. Cost optimisation measures introduced earlier in the year have started yielding results, helping the company manage expenses.

The company also reported growth opportunities following excise policy reforms in Karnataka, which supported the premium and above (P&A) segment. In Tamil Nadu, Mansion House Reserve Brandy recorded more than 25 percent sequential volume growth and 50 percent YoY growth in September, its highest-volume month to date.

During the quarter, TI entered the tequila category through a strategic investment in Black Tiger Distilleries, the maker of Bodega Suprema No. 5. The company also plans to expand its luxury and super-premium portfolio, with new launches expected from FY28 onwards.

Dahanukar said the company would focus on profitable growth across its core brands while expanding into higher-priced categories. He added that TI would use Imperial Blue's distribution network to introduce products across premium price segments.

The company's performance comes as it continues to integrate its expanded whisky portfolio while managing input-cost inflation and pursuing growth in premium spirits.

![Godrej Consumer Products Q2 Profit Rises 14 Pc to Rs 523 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/wdejdenefnfeh.jpg)

Godrej Consumer Products Limited (GCPL) reported a 14 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 523 crore for the second quarter of FY27, supported by 19 percent revenue growth and an 8 percent rise in underlying volume. ***The company announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, with consolidated sales growth across India and its international markets.***

Consolidated EBITDA, including forex, increased 12 percent year-on-year during the quarter. ***The company’s standalone business recorded 13 percent sales growth, backed by 7 percent underlying volume growth.*** Sales in Indonesia rose 20 percent, while the Africa, USA and Middle East (GAUM) business registered 40 percent growth in rupee terms.

> Aasif Malbari, Managing Director and CEO of GCPL said, “***Q2 FY27 has been a quarter of strong, broad-based performance for Godrej Consumer Products Limited, fully aligned with our expectations and strategic priorities. We delivered strong broad-based underlying volume growth across India, Indonesia and Africa, despite subdued monsoon conditions in India while supported by tailwinds in Indonesia.***”

***The company’s standalone business reported revenue of Rs 2,631 crore, up 13 percent year-on-year, while EBITDA increased 8 percent to Rs 553 crore.*** The performance came despite an estimated impact of around 150 basis points from trade inventory correction during the quarter. Among its domestic categories, Home Care recorded 19 percent value growth, led by air fresheners and home care liquids. GCPL also reported market share gains in household insecticides despite weak monsoon conditions. Its air freshener portfolio continued to grow, while Godrej Fab maintained its double-digit growth trajectory in fabric care.

***The company expanded its Home Care portfolio with the introduction of Godrej Rizz, a liquid dishwash product launched in select markets across West and South India.*** It also introduced Godrej Zap, marking its entry into the online stain remover segment. Godrej Spic, which was scaled nationally during the first quarter, continued to record sequential growth and consumer repeats.

Personal Care delivered 8 percent value growth during Q2 FY27. The soaps category remained stable despite price increases and reductions in grammage. ***Premium liquid formats, including Cinthol Bodywash, continued to gain traction, while the hair colour business sustained its growth momentum and reported market share gains across key products.*** Perfumes and deodorants also recorded double-digit growth, supported by demand for deodorants and premium fragrance formats.

GCPL’s international business remained a key contributor to its quarterly performance. Indonesia reported 20 percent sales growth and 8 percent underlying volume growth. EBITDA in the market increased 12 percent despite a sharp rise in LPG prices. The GAUM business, covering Africa, the USA and the Middle East, reported 40 percent sales growth in rupee terms and 23 percent in constant-currency terms. Underlying volume growth stood at 16 percent, while EBITDA increased 43 percent. The business has now recorded seven consecutive quarters of double-digit revenue growth and 11 consecutive quarters of double-digit profit growth.

***The company also highlighted rising input costs during the quarter, particularly in crude-linked derivatives, palm oil and other commodities.*** GCPL said inflation had created significant cost pressures across its India and Indonesia portfolios. In response, it has taken pricing measures, increased cost-saving initiatives and optimised media and trade investments.

Further calibrated price increases are expected in soaps and liquid detergents, where cost pressures remain high. Despite these challenges, GCPL retained its FY27 growth outlook. The company expects high-single-digit underlying volume growth in its standalone business, along with double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth at the consolidated level.

Trent Limited, the Tata Group's retail arm, reported a 23 percent year-on-year increase in standalone revenue from operations to Rs 5,788 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with the corresponding quarter last year. ***Operating EBITDA grew 37 percent to Rs 791 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) increased 9 percent to Rs 490 crore.***

The company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 22 percent to Rs 5,873 crore during the quarter. ***Consolidated operating EBITDA increased 37 percent to Rs 785 crore, while PAT grew 25 percent to Rs 468 crore.*** For the first half of FY27, Trent's standalone revenue increased 21 percent to Rs 11,454 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 37 percent to Rs 1,638 crore, while PAT grew 17 percent to Rs 1,021 crore. EBITDA grew 35 percent to Rs 1,633 crore, while PAT increased 24 percent to Rs 986 crore. ***The consolidated revenue figures exclude Trent Hypermarket's revenue, which is accounted for through the equity method.*** Trent continued to expand its fashion retail network during the quarter, with its value fashion brand Zudio crossing the 1,000-store milestone. The company also opened 10 Westside stores and 19 Zudio outlets during Q2 FY27, while consolidating two Zudio stores.

As of September 30, 2026, Trent operated 311 Westside stores, 999 Zudio stores, including seven outlets in the UAE, and 32 stores across its other lifestyle concepts. Its overall fashion retail footprint exceeded 18.5 million sq ft across 339 cities. ***The company's emerging categories, including beauty and personal care, innerwear and footwear, contributed more than 21 percent of its revenue, indicating the growing contribution of categories beyond its core fashion business.*** Westside's online business also recorded 20 percent growth during H1 FY27 and contributed more than 6 percent of the brand's total revenue, reflecting the contribution of its digital sales channel.

Trent's Star food and grocery business reported revenue growth of more than 20 percent in Q2 FY27. The company added one store during the quarter, taking its total network to 87 outlets across 13 cities. ***Private-label products accounted for more than 74 percent of Star's revenue, highlighting the contribution of its in-house product portfolio to the grocery business.***

***Chairman Noel N Tata highlighted the company's plans to expand its presence in Tier ll and Tier lll markets while continuing investments in its retail network.*** He also pointed to the growth opportunities within the Star food and grocery business.

With expansion across Westside, Zudio and Star, Trent continues to increase its presence across fashion, lifestyle and grocery retail categories. Its latest quarterly performance reflects growth in both its store network and online business, alongside an increasing contribution from emerging consumer categories.

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Retail India News: Blue Star Q2 Revenue Rises 21 Pc to Rs 2,931 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/ejbvfbcdh.jpg)

Blue Star Limited reported a 21 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 2,930.95 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,422.37 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. ***Alongside its financial results, the air-conditioning and refrigeration company announced the appointment of Nithianand S and Senthil Thangam as senior management personnel, effective November 1, 2026.***

The appointments were approved by the company's board on October 29, following recommendations from the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. ***The move comes as Blue Star looks to improve profitability through procurement savings, product cost optimisation and operational efficiencies amid rising input costs.***

Nithianand S, Group President, Supply Chain and Procurement, joined Blue Star in March 2021 and brings more than two decades of industry experience, including previous stints at Samsung Electronics and Whirlpool India. He has helped improve the growth and profitability of the company's room air-conditioner business through procurement initiatives, vendor consolidation, alternate sourcing, and e-procurement.

***Senthil Thangam, President of the Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Solutions Group, joined Blue Star in 1995 as a graduate engineer trainee.*** With over 30 years of experience across sales, marketing, and product management, he has been involved in developing and introducing several commercial air-conditioning products, including inverter VRF systems, inverter ducted machines, configured screw chillers, side-discharge VRF systems, and centrifugal chillers.

***Blue Star Q2 Financial Performance***

Blue Star's operating profit, calculated as EBITDA excluding other income, increased 10.5 percent to Rs 202.58 crore in Q2 FY27. However, its operating margin declined to 6.9 percent from 7.6 percent in the year-ago quarter, reflecting pressure from higher material costs and limited price adjustments.

Net profit increased 25.4 percent to Rs 123.91 crore from Rs 98.78 crore in Q2 FY26. ***The quarterly profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 23.02 crore from the sale of the company's MedTech business.*** Profit before tax, excluding exceptional items and the share of profit or loss from joint ventures, stood at Rs 133.61 crore, compared with Rs 133.16 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue increased 16.7 percent to Rs 6,308.87 crore. However, operating profit declined to Rs 377.53 crore from Rs 383.41 crore in H1 FY26. Net profit for the six-month period stood at Rs 226.42 crore, compared with Rs 219.60 crore a year earlier.

The company recognised exceptional income of Rs 32.19 crore during the first half, comprising Rs 23.02 crore from the sale of its MedTech business and Rs 9.17 crore from the sale of property. ***Blue Star's Unitary Products segment, which includes room air-conditioners and commercial refrigeration, recorded a 29.4 percent increase in revenue to Rs 897.66 crore during Q2 FY27.*** An extended summer season and delayed monsoon supported demand for room air-conditioners during the quarter.

***However, the segment's result declined to Rs 20.74 crore, equivalent to 2.3 percent of revenue, compared with Rs 42.72 crore or 6.2 percent in the year-ago period.*** The company attributed the pressure to rising material costs, which were not fully offset by periodic price increases. Blue Star is working on product portfolio rationalisation through differentiated models with optimised costs to improve margins. Its commercial refrigeration business has also started seeing a recovery in demand, although profitability remains under pressure.

The Electro-Mechanical Projects, Commercial Air Conditioning Systems, Service and International Business segment reported a 16.3 percent increase in revenue to Rs 1,935.99 crore. However, its segment result declined to Rs 133.15 crore from Rs 147.14 crore in Q2 FY26. ***Within the electro-mechanical projects business, data centres accounted for a significant share of order inflows, while enquiries from the factory segment remained strong.*** However, project execution delays affected billing growth during the quarter.

The Professional Electronics and Industrial Systems segment recorded a 51.2 percent increase in revenue to Rs 97.30 crore. Its segment result rose to Rs 23.10 crore from Rs 6.17 crore, partly supported by the reversal of warranty provisions following the MedTech business divestment.

***Order Book and Business Outlook***

Blue Star's carried-forward order book stood at Rs 7,229.22 crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with Rs 7,120.44 crore a year earlier. The company ended the quarter with a net cash position of Rs 289.43 crore, against net borrowings of Rs 417.06 crore as of September 30, 2025.

***Chairman and Managing Director Vir S Advani said the company continued to witness demand for room air-conditioners during the festive season.*** He also expects a strong pipeline of data centre mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) projects to translate into higher order inflows in the coming months. Demand across commercial air-conditioning and commercial refrigeration businesses has also shown signs of recovery.

However, Advani highlighted the possibility of a deficient monsoon, its impact on agricultural incomes and higher interest rates as factors that could affect near-term consumer demand. He also noted that the conclusion of the US trade deal and resolution of the West Asia crisis could support business growth. Blue Star expects to maintain its revenue growth momentum in the second half of FY27, with a focus on improving profitability through calibrated price increases, product cost optimisation and operational efficiencies.

Raymond Lifestyle Limited reported a 14 percent year-on-year increase in total income to Rs 2,125 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,865 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. ***The company's performance was supported by growth in branded apparel, higher demand for premium products and an improvement in international garmenting business.***

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the company's EBITDA increased 4 percent to Rs 270 crore from Rs 259 crore in Q2 FY26. However, its EBITDA margin declined to 12.7 percent from 13.9 percent a year earlier. ***Profit before tax (PBT), excluding exceptional items, stood at Rs 91 crore, down 16 percent from Rs 108 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.***

For the first half of FY27, Raymond Lifestyle recorded total income of Rs 3,685 crore, registering 10 percent growth compared with Rs 3,340 crore in H1 FY26. EBITDA increased 6 percent to Rs 404 crore from Rs 381 crore, while the EBITDA margin stood at 11 percent against 11.4 percent in the previous year. PBT before exceptional items declined 37 percent to Rs 53 crore from Rs 83 crore.

***Raymond Lifestyle's Branded Textile segment reported revenue of Rs 971 crore in Q2 FY27, registering 7 percent growth from Rs 906 crore in the year-ago quarter.*** The performance was supported by festive demand and the sale of premium products. Segment EBITDA remained largely stable at Rs 188 crore compared with Rs 186 crore in Q2 FY26. However, the EBITDA margin declined to 19.3 percent from 20.6 percent, reflecting higher raw material and freight costs.

The Branded Apparel segment recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 559 crore, up 20 percent from Rs 465 crore in Q2 FY26. Casualwear brands ColorPlus and Parx contributed to the segment's growth, outperforming broader apparel categories. EBITDA increased to Rs 49 crore from Rs 41 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The EBITDA margin remained at 8.8 percent, as higher raw material costs and an unfavourable channel mix affected profitability. The closure of underperforming stores helped offset some of the pressure.

The Garmenting business recorded one of the strongest performances during the quarter, with revenue increasing 26 percent to Rs 339 crore from Rs 269 crore in Q2 FY26. The growth was supported by order execution following the US-India tariff rationalisation, the UK-India Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and the addition of new international clients. ***EBITDA for the segment rose to Rs 25 crore from Rs 14 crore, while its margin improved to 7.4 percent from 5.3 percent, representing an expansion of 207 basis points year-on-year.***

Meanwhile, the High Value Cotton Shirting segment reported revenue of Rs 222 crore, up 5 percent from Rs 212 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. However, EBITDA declined to Rs 21 crore from Rs 25 crore, while the EBITDA margin fell to 9.5 percent from 12 percent. Higher raw material prices affected profitability, partly offset by improved average selling prices.

Raymond Lifestyle's Emerging Businesses, which include Ethnix by Raymond, Raymond Home, Park Avenue Innerwear, Chairman's Collections and Sexual Wellness, recorded revenue of Rs 100 crore in Q2 FY27, growing 15 percent from Rs 87 crore in the year-ago period. ***The company continued to review its retail network, focusing on store productivity and operational efficiency.*** Raymond Lifestyle had 1,634 stores at the end of September 2026, compared with 1,663 stores as of September 30, 2025. The company is reallocating resources towards more productive retail formats while allowing recently opened outlets to establish their operations.

Its financial position also improved during the reporting period. Raymond Lifestyle reported a net cash position of Rs 69 crore in September 2026, compared with net debt of Rs 246 crore in September 2025, reflecting cash generation of more than Rs 300 crore. The company also outlined its environmental, social and governance (ESG) targets for 2030. ***These include achieving 40 percent female representation, transitioning 25 percent of its electricity consumption to renewable sources and reducing Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 15 percent. It also aims to implement Zero Liquid Discharge and Zero Waste to Landfill initiatives.***

> Satyaki Ghosh, Wholetime Director and CEO of Raymond Lifestyle Limited said, “***Our performance in Q2 and H1 FY27 demonstrates sustained operational continuity, strategic resilience, and focused commercial execution across domestic and international markets. Our Garmenting business continued to deliver robust growth, capitalizing on global supply chain realignments, while our Branded Apparel business expanded by 20 percent, spearheaded by strong momentum across our casual brands ColorPlus and Parx. While elevated input costs and channel mix dynamics influenced near-term operating margins, our disciplined pricing, substantial working capital contraction, net debt-free balance sheet with Rs 69 crore in net cash provide tremendous operational resilience. As we enter the peak festive and wedding season, domestic demand indicators remain strong. Supported by retail network optimization, brand investments, and capacity ramp-ups, we remain firmly confident in our strategic direction and on track to achieve our stated FY27 guidance.***”

![Starbucks India Revenue Crosses Rs 1,367 Cr as Loss Narrows in FY26](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-30T115653.998.jpg)

Tata Starbucks, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata Consumer Products and Starbucks Corporation, continues to expand its presence in India's organised coffee market. **Despite establishing itself as one of the country's largest coffee chains in terms of revenue and store network, the company is yet to turn profitable.**

**Tata Starbucks recorded revenue from operations of Rs 1,367 crore in FY26, registering a year-on-year growth of 7 percent from Rs 1,277 crore in FY25.**

**Incorporated in September 2011, the company operates its cafes across India under the Starbucks brand. By 2025, its network had grown to more than 390 stores across 54 cities, supported by approximately 4,300 partners (employees).** The company has set an expansion target of around 1,000 stores by 2028.

**Sales of coffee and associated products remained the primary contributor to its operating revenue.** A smaller share came from its loyalty programme, My Starbucks Rewards, which allows customers to collect Stars on eligible purchases.

**On the expenditure front, the purchase of coffee beans and other related products accounted for nearly 24 percent of the company's total spending.** This expense increased 6 percent to Rs 356 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 336 crore in the previous fiscal. Employee benefit expenses also climbed 9.8 percent to Rs 225 crore during the year.

Other operating costs, including rent, electricity, advertising, freight and administrative overheads, contributed to a 4.7 percent rise in total expenses. **The company's overall expenditure stood at Rs 1,514 crore in FY26, up from Rs 1,446 crore in FY25.**

Despite the increase in operating costs, Tata Starbucks managed to reduce its net loss by 27 percent to Rs 99 crore in FY26 from Rs 136 crore in the previous fiscal. Its EBITDA stood at Rs 234 crore during the year.

**At the unit level, the company incurred Rs 1.11 in expenditure for every rupee generated through operating revenue.** Its standalone return on capital employed (ROCE) was recorded at -2.6 percent, while its EBITDA margin stood at 17 percent.

**Among its established competitors, Café Coffee Day reported revenue of Rs 1,094 crore and a net profit of Rs 14 crore.** Tata Starbucks also faces competition from a growing number of speciality and emerging coffee brands, including Blue Tokai, Rage Coffee, Third Wave Coffee Roasters, Slay Coffee, Sleepy Owl and Seven Beans Co.

![Vashi Mart to Add 22 Solar Equipment Outlets by FY27](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/decnncejun.jpg)

Vashi Integrated Solutions Ltd. plans to establish 22 Vashi Mart outlets across 10 states by FY 2026-27, expanding its distribution network for solar equipment and rooftop solar installation supplies in India. ***The initiative aims to improve access to solar products, inventory and technical support for installers, particularly in Tier ll and Tier lll markets.***

The counter-format distribution network is designed to address procurement challenges faced by rooftop solar installers, including fragmented sourcing and inconsistent product availability. ***Through Vashi Mart, the company intends to bring solar equipment and installation essentials closer to project locations, reducing the need for installers to purchase components from multiple suppliers.***

The expansion comes as India's rooftop solar market grows, supported by government initiatives such as the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. However, sourcing materials efficiently remains a challenge for installers working across different locations. Vashi Mart will offer a range of solar products and installation supplies at local outlets to help address these gaps.

The first phase will cover Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Uttarakhand and Odisha. Locations have been selected based on installer demand and rooftop solar potential, including district-level data associated with the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. ***Vashi Integrated Solutions aims to use the planned network to improve the availability of solar equipment as rooftop installations expand across the country.*** The company is positioning the initiative around local inventory access, supported by its existing distribution and warehousing infrastructure.

Each Vashi Mart will allow installers to purchase available products directly from the counter. Larger orders and project-specific requirements will be handled through the company's wider distribution network. The company will also integrate the outlets with DigiServe, its digital procurement platform. ***Through the platform, installers will be able to check inventory availability across locations, order products that are not available at a particular Mart, track deliveries and access product catalogues and technical information.***

Product guidance, practical training and technical assistance will form part of the offering, helping installers understand different solar products and technologies. The combination of physical outlets and digital procurement is intended to support purchasing requirements across multiple project locations. The network will primarily cater to residential rooftop solar installations, while also serving installers working on small commercial and industrial projects. Larger commercial and industrial solar requirements will continue to be supported through Vashi's fulfilment centres.

> Suraj Dodeja, Managing Director and Group CEO of Vashi Integrated Solutions Ltd said, “***India’s transition towards greater solar adoption requires not only strong policy support and growing consumer participation, but also an efficient distribution ecosystem that enables installers to execute projects with greater ease. Through Vashi Mart, we aim to strengthen this ecosystem by bringing solar products, installation essentials and technical support closer to installers across markets. By combining local inventory with digital ordering and technical support, we aim to simplify procurement and support installers as rooftop solar adoption expands across more markets.***”

Founded in 1978, Vashi Integrated Solutions operates in industrial supply and distribution. ***The company has a network of more than 22 hubs across over 100 cities and partnerships with over 65 international brands.*** Its solar business has been serving installers and engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) companies for a decade. The experience and existing distribution infrastructure are expected to support the planned expansion of Vashi Mart across multiple states.

With the proposed network, Vashi Integrated Solutions is seeking to strengthen last-mile distribution for rooftop solar equipment and make procurement more accessible for installers as India's solar installation market expands.

![Meesho Net Loss Narrows to Rs 132 Cr in Q2 FY27](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/csjcdbdcbd.jpg)

Meesho Reports Rs 12,911 Crore NMV in Q2 FY27Meesho reported a 23 percent year-on-year increase in Net Merchandise Value (NMV) to Rs 12,911 crore in the second quarter of FY27, while its net loss narrowed 68 percent to Rs 132 crore, according to the company's financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. ***The e-commerce marketplace recorded 819 million placed orders during the quarter, up 17 percent year-on-year.*** Its annual transacting user base grew 21 percent to 284 million, while annual purchase frequency increased 7 percent to 10.4 transactions per user, indicating higher repeat engagement on the platform.

First-time buyers increased 16 percent quarter-on-quarter, reflecting continued growth in Meesho's customer base ahead of the festive shopping season.

> Vidit Aatrey, Chairman, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer at Meesho said, "***Our Q2 performance reflects the strength of Meesho's operating model, with NMV growing 23 percent year-on-year to Rs 12,911 crore and Annual Transacting Users reaching 284 million. More consumers are shopping on Meesho, and they are shopping more frequently, even as first-time buyers grew 16 percent quarter-on-quarter. This momentum extended into the festive season, with NMV growing 33 percent year-on-year on a festive-aligned basis, reinforcing our conviction in the depth of India's e-commerce opportunity. As we grow, the benefits of scale are increasingly translating into stronger platform economics. Contribution Margin expanded to 6.0 percent of NMV, driven by logistics efficiencies and improved monetisation. At the same time, AI is fundamentally changing how we build and operate Meesho, with engineering productivity increasing 171 percent between March and September 2026. Our focus remains on reinvesting these efficiency gains into better consumer and seller experiences, accelerating innovation and building a larger, more efficient marketplace that can generate sustainable free cash flow over the long term.***"

Meesho's festive-aligned NMV grew 33 percent year-on-year over the 90 days preceding Dussehra. ***The company attributed the growth to demand across comparable festive periods.*** The comparison accounts for the Mega Blockbuster Sale shifting from the second quarter last year to the third quarter this year.

The company's branded commerce business also recorded growth during the quarter. Meesho Mall, which hosts approximately 1,800 brands, reported an 81 percent year-on-year increase in NMV. Growth reached 89 percent in Tier lll and smaller cities. ***Around half of Meesho Mall's customers during the quarter were first-time buyers on the platform's branded shopping section, with demand extending to categories such as beauty and personal care.*** Content commerce continued to expand, with NMV rising 160 percent year-on-year. The number of active order-generating content pieces increased 144 percent to 2.2 million, reflecting the growing role of creator-led product discovery in online shopping.

Meesho also reported an increase in seller participation. ***Annual transacting sellers grew 60 percent year-on-year to 1.13 million, while more than 4 lakh sellers became part of its content commerce ecosystem.*** Marketplace revenue from operations rose 34 percent year-on-year to Rs 4,120 crore, supported by higher advertising monetisation and improved matching of seller demand with consumer interest. Contribution margin increased to 6.0 percent of NMV, compared with 4.6 percent in the previous quarter.

Operational improvements also contributed to faster deliveries. Meesho said delivery times improved by approximately 15 percent year-on-year, supported by greater network density, better routing and partner allocation, and enhancements to its Geo-India system. Artificial intelligence has become a key part of the company's engineering and marketplace operations. ***Engineering productivity increased 171 percent between March and September 2026, while the number of experiments rose 73 percent.*** Approximately 65 percent of engineering pods were operating with a single engineer directing AI agents.

AI-powered development and code reviews reduced feature development timelines from weeks to days, while code approval times fell 41 percent. The company also reduced the time required to take a data science model to live testing from 17 days to three days through AI data science agents. Enhancements to Geo-India and TrustMesh were aimed at improving address intelligence, delivery efficiency and fraud detection.

On the financial front, Meesho generated Rs 345 crore in quarterly free cash flow, compared with an outflow of Rs 226 crore in the previous quarter. The company attributed the improvement partly to seasonal working capital benefits. ***Net loss declined to Rs 132 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 411 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.*** As of September 30, 2026, Meesho reported a cash balance of Rs 7,048 crore.

The results highlight growth in Meesho's e-commerce transaction volumes, customer engagement and seller base, alongside improvements in operating margins and losses. The company's performance also reflects the contribution of festive demand, branded commerce, creator-led shopping and technology investments to its marketplace operations.

Radico Khaitan Limited has appointed its Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Dilip K. Banthiya, as Whole-time Director on its Board, designating him as Executive Director and CFO. **The company has also elevated Saket Somani to Deputy Chief Financial Officer. Both appointments will take effect from October 28, 2026.**

**The leadership changes are aimed at strengthening the company's governance structure and financial management as it advances its premiumisation strategy and expands its global presence.** Banthiya's appointment to the Board will bring his experience in finance, capital allocation and the alcoholic beverages industry to the company's senior decision-making body.

Somani's elevation will broaden his responsibilities across financial strategy, planning, investor relations, capital markets and information technology. T**he revised structure is intended to strengthen the finance function and support the company's next phase of growth.**

> **Abhishek Khaitan, Managing Director, Radico Khaitan said,** “Earlier this year, we elevated leaders who have grown with Radico Khaitan. Today, we take that philosophy to the Board. Dilip has been central to our transformation, and his voice at the Board will sharpen our financial strategy and governance as we scale our premium portfolio and invest for the future. Saket brings a market-facing and technology-led approach that defines the next generation of financial leadership. Together, they give us experience at the top and depth beneath it, the foundation we need for the decade ahead.”

**Under the new structure, the Executive Director and CFO will oversee the company's financial direction and governance at the Board level.** The Deputy CFO will focus on financial planning, investor engagement and the organisation's digital transformation. The division of responsibilities is expected to support financial decision-making and operational priorities as the company pursues its growth plans.

> **Saket Somani, Deputy CFO, Radico Khaitan shared,** “I am grateful to the leadership for this opportunity. Over the past six years, I have had the privilege of working across the breadth of the finance function, from manufacturing finance and internal controls to operational performance and investor relations. Our aim now is to make finance a true strategic partner to the business, using technology and data to enable better-informed decisions. I look forward to working closely with Mr. Banthiya and the leadership team to support Radico Khaitan’s growth and global ambitions.”

**Somani brings around 20 years of experience in corporate finance, strategy, capital markets, investor relations and investment banking.** A Chartered Accountant, he joined Radico Khaitan in 2020 and most recently served as Senior Vice President – Finance and Strategy.

**During his tenure, Somani has overseen financial planning and control, working capital management, and the assessment of capital projects and new business opportunities.** He has also worked with the leadership team on strategic priorities, including growth and portfolio development. In addition, he has led the company's investor relations programme, strengthening engagement with institutional investors and improving its visibility in capital markets.

Sky Gold and Diamonds Limited, a listed B2B gold jewellery manufacturer, reported a 61 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 2,390.7 crore for the second quarter of FY27, ended September 30, 2026. ***EBITDA rose 90 percent to Rs 189.8 crore, while reported profit after tax (PAT) increased 93.2 percent to Rs 129.4 crore.***

For the first half of FY27, the company's consolidated revenue grew 68.3 percent year-on-year to Rs 4,403.5 crore. EBITDA more than doubled, rising 102.3 percent to Rs 346.5 crore, while reported PAT increased 111.9 percent to Rs 234.3 crore. ***The company's EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 improved to 7.94 percent from 6.7 percent in the corresponding quarter last year.*** For H1 FY27, the margin stood at 7.87 percent, compared with 6.5 percent in H1 FY26.

Reported profit before tax (PBT) for the second quarter rose 88.9 percent year-on-year to Rs 166 crore. For the first half, reported PBT increased 105 percent to Rs 300.8 crore.

> Mangesh Chauhan, Managing Director of Sky Gold and Diamonds Limited said, “***For the half year ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported consolidated revenue of Rs 4,403.5 crore, EBITDA of Rs 346.5 crore and profit after tax of Rs 234.3 crore. For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, consolidated revenue was Rs 2,390.7 crore, EBITDA was Rs 189.8 crore and profit after tax was Rs 129.4 crore.***”

Sky Gold and Diamonds also reported an improvement in its profit margins during the quarter. ***The reported PAT margin increased to 5.4 percent in Q2 FY27 from 4.5 percent in Q2 FY26. For the first half, the margin rose to 5.3 percent from 4.2 percent in the year-ago period.*** Operational PBT for Q2 FY27 increased 97.3 percent year-on-year to Rs 173.4 crore, while operational PAT rose 106.8 percent to Rs 138.56 crore. For H1 FY27, operational PBT increased 110 percent to Rs 308.2 crore, and operational PAT grew 120.2 percent to Rs 234.5 crore. The company calculates operational profit after excluding non-operational income included under other income in its financial statements.

***Cash flow from operations stood at Rs 136.7 crore in H1 FY27, compared with an outflow of Rs 100.9 crore in the corresponding period of the previous year, according to the company's financial update.*** Cash flow from operations as a proportion of EBITDA reached 39 percent, against the company's earlier guidance of 20 percent.

The company also announced progress on its acquisition of Purvi Gems and Jewellery (India) Private Limited. ***On October 7, 2026, its board approved the completion of the acquisition of a 100 percent stake in the company for a total cash consideration of Rs 9 crore.*** The latest results reflect growth in Sky Gold and Diamonds' revenue, operating earnings and profitability during the first half of FY27, alongside an improvement in operating cash flow and the completion of a planned acquisition in the jewellery sector.

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)

![LT Foods Reports 22 Pc Revenue Growth to Rs 6,414 Cr in H1 FY27](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/dehcbefne.jpg)

LT Foods, the company behind the Daawat and Royal rice brands, reported a 22 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 6,414 crore for the first half of FY27, ended September 30, 2026. ***Consolidated EBITDA rose 17 percent to Rs 721 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) increased 9 percent to Rs 364 crore.***

The company announced its unaudited consolidated financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, reporting growth across its rice business and key international markets.

> Ashwani Arora, Managing Director and CEO of LT Foods said, “***We delivered a strong performance in the first half of FY’27, reflecting the strength of our brands, the resilience of our diversified global business and disciplined execution across markets. For H1 FY’27, our consolidated revenue grew 22 percent year-on-year to Rs 6,414 crore (Normalized Growth 18 percent including Golden Star), EBITDA increased 17 percent to Rs 721 crore, and PAT grew 9 percent to Rs 364 crore. This performance reflects our continued focus on building strong consumer-focussed brands, driving premiumisation and innovation, and strengthening operational efficiencies across the business."***

### LT Foods Q2 FY27 Financial Performance

For the second quarter of FY27, LT Foods reported consolidated revenue of Rs 3,253 crore, up 17 percent year-on-year and 3 percent sequentially. EBITDA increased 13 percent year-on-year to Rs 358 crore, while PAT rose 10 percent to Rs 180 crore. ***For the first half, standalone revenue grew 14.1 percent year-on-year to Rs 2,417 crore. Standalone EBITDA increased 33.5 percent to Rs 223 crore, while PAT rose 23.9 percent to Rs 134 crore.***

Consolidated gross profit for H1 FY27 increased 15 percent to Rs 2,087 crore. However, the gross profit margin declined 190 basis points to 32.5 percent. The EBITDA margin fell 50 basis points to 11.2 percent, while the PAT margin decreased 60 basis points to 5.7 percent. ***The company attributed the margin movement to changes in shipment terms with related parties, the restructuring of its organic business and higher brand investments.***

### Basmati Rice Business Drives Growth

LT Foods' Basmati and Other Specialty Rice business recorded 27 percent year-on-year growth in H1 FY27. ***Including Golden Star, normalized growth stood at 22 percent.*** The Organic Foods and Ingredients segment reported revenue of around Rs 520 crore as the company continued to restructure the business. The segment also recorded an 11 percent decline on a year-on-year basis, according to the company's financial update.

Revenue from the Ready-to-Eat (RTE), Ready-to-Cook (RTC) and Ready-to-Heat (RTH) portfolio increased 8 percent to Rs 102 crore. The segment includes quick-cooking rice products, biryani kits, ready-to-heat offerings in the US and Japanese rice snacks.

### India Market Sees 24 percent Growth

India recorded 24 percent year-on-year growth for LT Foods in H1 FY27, making it a key contributor to the company's performance. ***Its strategy in the domestic market includes expanding distribution, introducing products, increasing premium offerings and strengthening operational capabilities.*** During the quarter, the company expanded its Daawat portfolio with Daawat Delight and Daawat Rozana Platinum. It also added Daawat Biryani Masala Paste to its biryani range.

The company's health-focused quick-cooking brown, red and black rice products recorded double-digit growth compared with the previous year. Daawat Quick Cooking Brown Rice maintained a market share of more than 70 percent in general trade and modern retail outlets, according to the company. ***Its Daawat I'm Organic range also continued to gain traction, accounting for nearly 18 percent of the organic rice segment on key e-commerce platforms.*** Daawat Biryani Kits recorded double-digit value growth in the first half and held more than 70 percent share on key e-commerce platforms.

LT Foods said its branded portfolio grew nearly 8 percent while the overall category expanded by approximately 1.3 percent. This helped the company increase its year-to-date market share by 140 basis points. ***Daawat's market share in India stood at 22.3 percent as of September 2026, based on the AC Nielsen Retail Survey Audit cited by the company.*** Its household reach increased to 67.5 lakh households, representing 20 percent growth over the preceding 12 months, according to the Kantar Household Panel data cited in its update.

The company also continued to expand its distribution network and invest in direct distribution, sales capabilities and supply chain digitisation to improve product availability across retail channels.

### North America and Other Global Markets

North America recorded 20.8 percent growth for LT Foods in H1 FY27. Normalized growth, including Golden Star, stood at 13.3 percent. Its Royal brand retained more than 60 percent market share, while Golden Star continued to hold the leading position in the US Jasmine rice category, according to the company. Golden Star also entered the ready-to-heat rice segment with microwaveable rice cups available in three varieties: Jasmine Rice, Coconut Jasmine Rice and Jasmine Fried Rice.

***In Europe, LT Foods continued to work on expanding distribution, strengthening retail partnerships and increasing brand presence, with initiatives in the Netherlands and Germany.*** Its UK business also reported growth across pack sizes and key Daawat categories through its independent and grocery channels.

The Middle East and other international markets recorded 24.6 percent year-on-year growth in H1 FY27. In the UAE, the company expanded its health-focused portfolio with Daawat Quick Cooking Black Rice and Daawat Quick Cooking Red Rice across premium retail outlets and e-commerce platforms. In Saudi Arabia, Daawat Mazza recorded its highest-ever offtakes at Othaim Retail.

### Nature Bio Foods Acquires Stake in Dutch Company

LT Foods' organic business arm, Nature Bio Foods, acquired a controlling stake in Netherlands-based Leev.nu B.V. through its subsidiary Nature Bio Foods B.V. The all-cash transaction was valued at €1.735 million.

Following the acquisition, Nature Bio Foods B.V.'s stake in Leev.nu B.V. stands at 70.75 percent.

The company also reported an improvement in its CRISIL ESG rating from 54 to 61, moving from the 'Adequate' to the 'Strong' category. Its sustainability initiatives cover farming practices, responsible sourcing, manufacturing, distribution and product development. LT Foods said digital transformation remains a priority, with investments in technology aimed at improving customer engagement, sales visibility, forecasting and operational efficiency. As the company enters the second half of FY27, it plans to continue focusing on its branded rice portfolio, international expansion, product innovation and distribution capabilities.

### LT Foods Financial Highlights for H1 FY27

* Consolidated revenue: Rs 6,414 crore, up 22 percent year-on-year
* EBITDA: Rs 721 crore, up 17 percent
* Profit after tax: Rs 364 crore, up 9 percent
* Gross profit: Rs 2,087 crore, up 15 percent
* India business growth: 24 percent
* Basmati and Other Specialty Rice growth: 27 percent
* North America growth: 20.8 percent
* Middle East and Rest of the World growth: 24.6 percent

Tata Consumer Products Ltd (TCPL) reported a 15.65 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 470.14 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 406.51 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. **Revenue from operations rose 14 percent to Rs 5,661.13 crore, driven by domestic volume growth, improved margins, price increases and input cost management.**

**TCPL Group CFO Ashish Goenka said the company benefited from stronger domestic demand and growth across its business portfolio.** “*We have a strong topline growth along with margin expansion, and I think profitability is going ahead of the topline. **The company implemented selective price increases to offset higher costs of tea, salt, freight and fuel.** Its India business recorded 17 percent value growth and 11 percent underlying volume growth, with pricing contributing around 5.5 to 6 percent. Its regular and speciality tea businesses in Canada continued to grow ahead of the market.

**As part of its retail expansion strategy, the company operates exclusive brand outlets and shop-in-shop (SIS) formats within P. N. Gadgil & Sons showrooms.** It is also developing its digital sales channels through a dedicated e-commerce platform, allowing customers to browse and purchase natural diamond jewellery online.

The company aims to strengthen its market presence through an expanded retail network, improved digital accessibility, and a focus on certified natural diamond jewellery. **These initiatives are intended to increase consumer access to its products and support its growth in the organised diamond jewellery segment.**

![HomeLane Turns EBITDA Positive in Q4 FY26 With Rs 212 Cr Revenue](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-27T145626.713.jpg)

HomeLane, a technology-enabled home interiors company, reported operating EBITDA profitability in Q4 FY26, with quarterly revenue of Rs 212 crore and an operating EBITDA margin of 5 percent. **The company also recorded 19 percent year-on-year revenue growth and a 37 percent increase in its order book during the first half of FY27, according to unaudited management figures.**

**Following the integration of HomeLane and DesignCafe, the company expects to cross Rs 1,000 crore in revenue in FY27 and achieve full-year EBITDA profitability.** Its order book growth, which outpaced revenue growth, is expected to support performance in the second half of the financial year as orders convert into revenue over six to nine months.

**FY26 was the first full financial year of combined operations for HomeLane and DesignCafe.** The company prioritised integration over revenue growth, with annual revenue remaining stable at Rs 745 crore. **However, direct project costs declined from 56.6 percent of revenue in FY25 to 52 percent in FY26, improving project margins by 460 basis points through consolidated sourcing, manufacturing and installation operations.**

HomeLane has also completed the amalgamation of G S E-Commerce Private Limited, which operates DesignCafe, into Homevista Decor and Furnishings Private Limited. **The group now operates both brands under a single legal entity, sharing technology, supply chain and operational infrastructure.**

**The company reported a loss before tax of Rs 137 crore in FY26, including Rs 19 crore in integration and one-time expenses.** Excluding these costs, the loss before tax stood at Rs 118 crore, in line with FY25.

> **Srikanth Iyer, Co-founder and CEO, HomeLane shared**, "Merging two companies is a lot like renovating a home while you’re still living in it. It gets dusty for a while, but you come out with a far better home. FY26 was the year we chose to build the foundation rather than chase the topline. Bringing HomeLane and DesignCafe together improved our project economics by 460 basis points and took us to EBITDA profitability in the fourth quarter. This year, revenue is up 19 percent and our order book is up 37 percent. Crossing Rs 1,000 Cr with a full year of EBITDA profitability is our next milestone, and our teams and franchise partners are making it happen one home at a time.”

![Snapdeal Parent AceVector Sees Revenue Growth and Higher Losses in Q2 FY27](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-27T123516.944.jpg)

AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal, reported a 17 percent year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 151.2 crore in Q2 FY27, marking its first quarterly results since its stock market listing earlier this month. **However, the company’s net loss increased 85 percent to Rs 17.6 crore.**

**AceVector's operating revenue stood at Rs 129.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.** Including Rs 2.6 crore in non-operating income, its total income reached Rs 153.8 crore during the quarter.

**Snapdeal's marketplace business contributed Rs 86.2 crore, accounting for 57 percent of operating revenue and registering 15 percent year-on-year growth.** Unicommerce, AceVector's e-commerce enablement software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform, generated Rs 59 crore, while its consumer brands business contributed Rs 6 crore.

**For the first half of FY27, AceVector's consolidated revenue increased 17 percent year-on-year to Rs 285.5 crore.** Snapdeal's revenue rose 15 percent to Rs 164.4 crore, while Unicommerce recorded a similar 15 percent increase to Rs 110.4 crore.

**Snapdeal's fashion net merchandise value (NMV) grew 31 percent year-on-year to Rs 407.6 crore in H1 FY27.** Its annual transacting customer base increased 12 percent to 130.8 lakh, while app-delivered units rose 23 percent to 133.6 lakh. During the period, the marketplace also introduced an artificial intelligence (AI) solutions suite offering features for product discovery, personalised recommendations, and seller support.

**AceVector's total expenditure increased more than 21 percent to Rs 168.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 138.7 crore a year earlier.** Logistics remained its largest expense at Rs 71.4 crore, up 20 percent year-on-year, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 46 crore. **The reported loss included Rs 1.3 crore in exceptional items.**

**AceVector's Rs 420 crore initial public offering (IPO) received approximately five times subscription but made a weak stock market debut.** Shares listed at an 11.5 percent discount to the IPO price of Rs 32, opening at Rs 28.32 on the NSE and Rs 28.30 on the BSE.

**The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 133 crore, with a price band of Rs 30 to Rs 32 per share.** At Monday's market close, AceVector shares stood at Rs 20.92, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 1,138 crore.

Swiss Beauty, an Indian cosmetics brand, has partnered with Paris Fashion Week to showcase its makeup products on the international runway. As part of the association, the brand created eight makeup looks using its products, featured on six models and two influencers.

The partnership marks a step in Swiss Beauty’s efforts to expand its presence beyond India and strengthen its association with the global fashion and beauty industry. The collaboration brings the brand’s products into the runway creative process, positioning makeup as an integral part of fashion presentation and self-expression.

According to the company, the initiative reflects its ambition to explore new platforms for showcasing its products beyond conventional marketing and consumer engagement channels.

Commenting on the association, Mohit, Founder, Swiss Beauty, said the brand’s participation at Paris Fashion Week represents an important milestone in its growth journey and reflects its ambitions for the future.

He added that the platform offers the brand an opportunity to take its makeup expertise to an international fashion audience.

##### **Swiss Beauty Focuses on Creative Makeup and Global Exposure**

The eight runway looks were designed to highlight the versatility of Swiss Beauty’s products across different styles and creative expressions. The brand said the initiative allowed its products to become part of the show's creative process rather than serving solely as a branding element.

Shalini, AVP – Marketing, Swiss Beauty, said the partnership was significant because the brand’s products were used to develop the runway looks. She added that the eight looks demonstrated different applications of its makeup range and reflected the brand’s focus on self-expression.

The collaboration also brought Swiss Beauty’s brand philosophy, “We Got You”, to an international fashion platform.

Gresha Sen Gupta, AVP – Creative Director, Swiss Beauty, said the association was an opportunity to connect fashion and beauty in a new setting. She added that the brand aimed to demonstrate its creative approach through different faces, looks and runway presentations.

##### **Expanding Beyond Traditional Beauty Marketing**

Swiss Beauty worked with Gold Coast to bring the partnership to life at Paris Fashion Week. The initiative forms part of the brand’s broader strategy to take its products beyond conventional brand and consumer touchpoints and into global fashion and cultural platforms.

By integrating its makeup products into a runway presentation, the brand aims to strengthen its positioning at the intersection of beauty, fashion and creative expression while reaching an international audience.

Myntra’s Big Fashion Festival (BFF) recorded nearly double the order volume of regular business days for direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, international labels, and its Gen Z-focused fashion platform FWD, according to the company. ***The event also expanded the reach of emerging brands, with visits increasing 25 percent compared with the previous edition and new customers from non-metro regions rising 74 percent over regular business days.***

Several Indian and international brands recorded strong demand during the fashion sale. ***These included RARE RABBIT, House of Pataudi, Glitchez, The Souled Store, SZN, CULT, Comet, Mamaearth and Minimalist.*** International brands that saw traction included MANGO, H&M, NEXT, Mothercare, ALDO, GAP, GUESS, Michael Kors, Fossil, Gymshark, Women's Secret, adidas and Nike.

Myntra has onboarded 12,000 sellers so far in 2026, giving emerging businesses from cities such as Surat, Ludhiana, Kolkata and Delhi-NCR access to customers across India. ***During the Big Fashion Festival, one in four sellers recorded a twofold increase in sales, while more than 1,350 sellers reported a fivefold rise.***

***Non-metro markets contributed to customer acquisition during the event, with Guwahati, Dehradun, Bhubaneswar, Jammu and Gorakhpur emerging as the fastest-growing non-metro cities.*** Traffic on the first day also recorded a significant year-on-year increase, while men's casual wear accounted for 26 percent of all first-time buyers.

Festive shopping demand in eastern India, particularly West Bengal, Assam and Odisha, was higher than during the previous edition. Ethnic wear, footwear and beauty and personal care products contributed to the increase. Ethnic wear brands that recorded demand included Libas, Inddus, Soch, Koski and Aurelia.

Men's occasion wear, men's casual footwear, wearables, sports footwear, watches, eyewear, women's sports apparel, jewellery, luggage, travel and accessories were among the fastest-growing categories. ***Sports footwear orders increased 3.5 times compared with regular business days.*** Men's casual wear, personal care, women's ethnic wear, women's western wear and kidswear were among the categories with the highest demand.

Myntra Beauty also recorded an increase in customer acquisition, with new customers rising about 20 percent compared with the previous edition. ***Perfumes, face washes, cleansers, day creams and lipsticks were among the leading product categories. Brands including Lakme, Mamaearth, L'Oréal, Maybelline and Cetaphil recorded strong demand.***

Myntra's quick-commerce service, M-Now, recorded more than 2.6 times growth in orders compared with the previous Big Fashion Festival. ***Demand included kurta sets, T-shirts, shirts, tops, jeans, dresses, perfumes, lipsticks, sarees, lingerie and watches.*** Brands recording high demand on M-Now included MANGO, Allen Solly, USPA, Van Heusen, Trendyol, Puma, Underneath, Anouk, Sangria, HRX, Maybelline, Lakme and Minimalist.

The fastest M-Now delivery during the event took less than five minutes. The most expensive purchase was an international luxury jacket valued at more than Rs 1,90,000. The latest edition of the Big Fashion Festival highlighted demand across fashion, beauty, sportswear and lifestyle categories, while providing emerging sellers with access to a wider customer base through Myntra's online marketplace.

August Jewellery reported a turnover of Rs 97.93 crore in the financial year ended March 31, 2026. Its turnover stood at Rs 33.25 crore in FY2024-25, compared with Rs 173.63 crore in FY2023-24.
