![Wow! Momo Plans QSR Entry into Sri Lanka, Eyes UAE and US Markets](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Image%20%287%29.jpg)

Wow! Momo Foods is expanding beyond India as it looks to establish its quick-service restaurant (QSR) business in international markets while growing its packaged food portfolio overseas. The company plans to launch its first international QSR operations in Sri Lanka, while Wow! FMCG, which currently exports to 14 countries, is targeting the US, Malaysia, Australia, Thailand and Canada for further expansion.

The Sri Lanka entry will be undertaken through a master franchise partnership with Softlogic Corporation, a diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate. The company plans to open its first three outlets in Colombo across different formats, including Wow! Momo Asia at One Galle Face Mall, a food court outlet at Havelock City Mall and a standalone restaurant at Arcade Independence Square.

Wow! Momo Foods aims to expand its Sri Lankan network to 20 outlets within the first two years. The launch will also help the company understand local consumer preferences and develop an operating model for future international expansion.

> “When you build a brand in India, you naturally start wondering whether the same love for the product can travel beyond the country. But going global is not about assuming that what works here will automatically work everywhere. It is about listening, learning and adapting,” said Sagar Daryani, Co-founder and CEO, Wow! Momo Foods Pvt. Ltd.

### **UAE Next on QSR Roadmap**

Following Sri Lanka, the company is evaluating the UAE as its next international QSR market, with Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah under consideration. It is in discussions with potential partners and exploring joint venture and master franchise arrangements.

The US is also on the company's roadmap, with entry targeted after the next two years. The experience gained in Sri Lanka and the UAE is expected to help the company determine suitable menus, formats and partnerships before entering the market.

### **FMCG Business in 14 Countries**

While its restaurant business prepares for its first international entry, Wow! FMCG has already established an overseas presence across 14 countries, including the UAE, Oman, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Russia, Singapore, the UK, Ireland, Germany, Mauritius, Sri Lanka and New Zealand.

Its portfolio includes momos, noodles, cup noodles, smileys and kulfi, distributed through more than 1,000 international touchpoints across modern retail and e-commerce.

The FMCG business has partnered with LuLu Group International to expand its presence in the Middle East and other retail channels. It also works with Noon and Amazon Middle East, while Mustafa Centre serves as a retail partner in Singapore. Its products are also supplied to international restaurants, cafes, catering businesses and commercial kitchens.

> “Our FMCG journey has been built market by market, with a strong focus on understanding local consumer behaviour, building the right distribution partnerships and creating a portfolio that can scale across diverse markets,” said Mithun Appaiah, CEO, Wow! Sales Pvt. Ltd.

He added that the next phase would focus on entering new geographies, strengthening distribution in existing markets and expanding the company's retail, e-commerce and foodservice network.

The company is also in discussions with large international retail chains to widen its distribution. Its FMCG business is currently entirely focused on branded retail, reflecting its strategy of building consumer recognition across markets.

Founded in **2008**, Wow! Momo Foods has grown from a single kiosk into a multi-brand business with more than **900 stores** across over **100 Indian cities**. Its portfolio includes Wow! Momo, Wow! China, Wow! Chicken and Wow! Kulfi. The planned overseas expansion marks its next step towards building an international presence across restaurant and packaged food businesses.

![HomeLane Targets Rs 1,000 Cr Revenue in FY27 After Turning EBITDA Positive in Q4 FY26](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/homelane.jpg)

HomeLane, a technology-enabled home interiors company, is targeting revenue of more than ₹1,000 crore in FY27 after achieving operating EBITDA profitability in the fourth quarter of FY26. The company reported quarterly revenue of ₹212 crore and an operating EBITDA margin of 5% in Q4 FY26.

The company has also reported strong business momentum in the first half of FY27, with revenue growing 19% year on year and its order book increasing 37%, according to unaudited management figures.

HomeLane expects the growth in its order book to support revenue performance in the second half of FY27, as orders typically convert into revenue over the following six to nine months. Backed by a leaner cost structure and a growing project pipeline, the company is targeting full-year EBITDA profitability in FY27.

**HomeLane Improves Project Margins After Integration**

FY26 marked the first full financial year of HomeLane and DesignCafe operating together. During the year, the company prioritised integrating the two businesses over accelerating revenue growth, with revenue remaining stable at ₹745 crore.

The integration helped improve project economics, with direct project costs declining from 56.6% of revenue in FY25 to 52% in FY26. This 460-basis-point improvement was driven by the consolidation of sourcing, manufacturing partners and installation operations across the two brands.

HomeLane has also completed the amalgamation of G S E-Commerce Private Limited, which operates DesignCafe, into Homevista Decor and Furnishings Private Limited, the group's parent company. The business now operates as a single legal entity with HomeLane and DesignCafe continuing as separate consumer brands, supported by a common technology platform, supply chain and operating infrastructure.

##### **Loss Narrows on a Like-for-Like Basis**

HomeLane reported a loss before tax of ₹137 crore in FY26, compared with ₹111 crore in FY25. The FY26 figure included ₹19 crore in integration-related and one-time costs.

Excluding these expenses and other one-off items, the company's loss before tax stood at ₹118 crore in FY26, broadly in line with the previous financial year.

Commenting on the company's performance, Srikanth Iyer, Co-founder and CEO, HomeLane, said the integration of HomeLane and DesignCafe was a priority during FY26, helping improve project economics and achieve operating EBITDA profitability in the fourth quarter.

He added that the company has returned to growth in FY27, with revenue increasing 19% and the order book expanding 37% year on year in the first half. HomeLane is now focused on crossing ₹1,000 crore in revenue and achieving full-year EBITDA profitability, with support from its teams and franchise partners.

Contemporary fine jewellery brand Kicky & Perky has opened its first official store at DLF Midtown Plaza in Moti Nagar, New Delhi, marking its move towards expanding its physical retail presence. Founded in 2022 by sisters Aditi Khandelwal and Sanya Khandelwal, the brand currently operates through kiosks and is looking to bring its collections to more consumers through dedicated retail spaces. The store was inaugurated by Aditi Khandelwal, Founder of Kicky & Perky, and Rita Gangwani, Celebrity Pageant Coach, at a ribbon-cutting ceremony on October 23, 2026.

The new outlet offers customers an opportunity to explore the brand’s jewellery collections in person, with designs spanning everyday wear, statement pieces, occasion jewellery and men’s jewellery.

Kicky & Perky specialises in 925 sterling silver jewellery featuring moissanites and precious and semi-precious stones. Its collections draw inspiration from art, Indian culture, architecture, mythology and nature, combining these influences with contemporary designs.

The launch marks a step in the brand’s retail expansion, building on its existing kiosk presence with a dedicated store format. The physical outlet is intended to offer customers a closer look at the materials, craftsmanship and design details behind its collections.

> Commenting on the opening, Aditi Khandelwal, Founder of Kicky & Perky, said, “Opening our first official store is an important milestone for us, because it allows customers to experience Kicky & Perky beyond the digital space. We have always approached jewellery as a form of individual expression, where art, culture and craftsmanship come together in designs made for modern life. Our kiosks have helped us connect with customers, and this store gives that relationship a more personal dimension. As we grow, our focus remains on building a distinctive design-led brand and creating experiences that make our customers feel connected to the stories behind our pieces.”

The brand plans to open more stores as it looks to expand its retail footprint and reach a wider customer base.

Westlife Foodworld Limited, which operates McDonald's restaurants across West and South India through its wholly owned subsidiary Hardcastle Restaurants Pvt Ltd, reported a 16 percent year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 7.47 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Same-store sales growth (SSSG) reached 10.1 percent, supported by double-digit growth in customer visits.

The company's performance was supported by demand across sales channels and regions, along with its value offerings, menu changes and digital ordering services. Dine-in sales accounted for 59 percent of system sales, while McDelivery continued to contribute to the company's business. ***Westlife Foodworld also reported an improvement in operating profitability during the quarter. Operating EBITDA rose 29 percent year on year to Rs 981 million, while the EBITDA margin increased to 13.1 percent.*** Cash profit after tax (PAT) stood at Rs 526 million, representing a margin of 7.0 percent.

Westlife Foodworld added 11 McDonald's restaurants during the quarter, taking its network to 492 outlets across 80 cities in West and South India. ***The company is continuing to expand its restaurant footprint across existing and emerging markets, with a focus on improving customer access and convenience.*** The latest additions bring the business closer to its target milestone of 500 restaurants. Westlife Foodworld said its growth strategy combines restaurant expansion with improvements in customer experience, menu offerings and access to ordering channels.

> Amit Jatia, Chairperson of Westlife Foodworld Limited said, “***The results of the quarter reflect the strength of our strategy, the discipline of our execution and the enduring relevance of the McDonald's brand. Strong guest growth, improving profitability and continued market expansion position us well to capture the significant opportunity ahead, create long-term value and further strengthen our leadership in the industry.***”

Digital channels remained an important part of Westlife Foodworld's sales mix, contributing more than 75 percent of sales during the quarter. The McDonald's app ecosystem crossed 58 million cumulative downloads, while monthly active users reached approximately 4.2 million. ***The company continues to use its app, delivery services and other digital ordering options to improve customer engagement and make ordering more convenient.***

***Dine-in and delivery channels remain central to its omnichannel strategy, allowing customers to access McDonald's restaurants through both in-person visits and digital platforms.*** Westlife Foodworld is marking 30 years of McDonald's operations in West and South India. Over this period, the company has expanded its restaurant network alongside the growth of India's quick-service restaurant (QSR) industry.

With its network approaching 500 restaurants, Westlife Foodworld plans to continue investing in restaurant expansion, digital engagement and customer experience across the two regions. The latest quarterly results reflect growth in revenue, same-store sales and operating profitability, alongside continued investment in the company's physical restaurant network and digital sales channels.

Honasa Consumer Limited, the parent company of Mamaearth and other beauty and personal care brands, has elevated Vipul Maheshwari to Chief Product and Technology Officer (CPTO). In his new role, Maheshwari will oversee product, technology, engineering and analytics, with a focus on advancing the company's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy and developing agentic AI capabilities.

***Maheshwari has spent the past six years building Honasa's data and product capabilities, working across business intelligence, technology and product development.*** His new responsibilities will include turning these capabilities into scalable AI-powered systems to support decision-making, improve operational efficiency and streamline business processes.

As Honasa expands its beauty and personal care portfolio, the company is investing in AI tools and automated workflows to simplify operations and help teams make decisions faster. ***It is also exploring agentic AI systems that can coordinate tasks and execute multi-step workflows under appropriate human supervision.*** The company aims to integrate AI into its day-to-day operations rather than limit its use to individual applications. Maheshwari's experience in data analytics and product development is expected to support the development and implementation of these systems across the organisation.

> Varun Alagh, Co-Founder and CEO of Honasa Consumer Limited said, “***Technology has always been an important enabler of our growth, and AI presents an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how we build and operate our business. As we move towards a more intelligent and connected organisation, our ambition is to go beyond isolated use cases and build AI-powered workflows and agentic capabilities that help our teams operate with greater speed, precision and effectiveness. Vipul’s strong foundation in data and product, along with his deep understanding of our business, makes him well positioned to shape and lead this journey. His elevation reflects our commitment to building leadership from within and investing in capabilities that will define our next phase of growth.***”

***The company's AI strategy includes developing workflows that automate repetitive tasks, connect business processes and support operational decisions.*** Its proposed agentic AI systems are intended to handle multiple steps within a workflow, with human oversight built into their implementation. These initiatives form part of Honasa's efforts to use technology to manage its expanding business and improve coordination across its functions.

> Vipul Maheshwari, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Honasa Consumer Limited said, “***AI and agentic systems represent a fundamental shift in how businesses will operate, moving from tools that provide information to intelligent systems that can execute workflows, connect decisions and drive outcomes. At Honasa, our strong foundation in data and product gives us the opportunity to build an AI-first approach to solving business problems. We are focused on developing intelligent workflows, enabling AI agents to support multi-step processes with the right guardrails, and embedding intelligence into everyday operations. My priority will be to translate this vision into scalable capabilities that deliver measurable business impact, strengthen organisational agility and create lasting value.***”

***In his new position, Maheshwari will focus on developing AI-enabled systems that can be deployed across business functions.*** The company intends to use these capabilities to improve productivity, strengthen decision-making and support more efficient operations as its brand portfolio grows.

Maheshwari holds a master's degree in Mathematics and Computer Science from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. ***Before joining Honasa Consumer, he held key positions at Delhivery and Global Analytics India Pvt Ltd, where he worked on data-driven business solutions and analytics-led problem-solving.*** His elevation places product development, engineering, technology and analytics under a single leadership role as Honasa continues to develop its AI capabilities across the beauty and personal care business.

Swiggy reported increased demand for fasting foods and traditional sweets during the Navratri and Durga Puja festivities in India, with orders rising around Durga Ashtami, Maha Navami, and Dussehra. **The food delivery platform recorded higher demand for vrat specialities between October 17 and October 20, 2026, alongside a rise in orders for traditional Indian sweets.**

**Sabudana dishes emerged as the most ordered fasting food nationwide between October 17 and October 20, followed by Navratri vrat thalis, Singhara-based preparations, Kuttu and Rajgira specialities.** Samak rice and Makhana dishes also featured among popular fasting options.

**During the October 17-18 weekend, Swiggy delivered an average of 1,794 Sabudana dishes every hour across India.** Sabudana Khichdi and Sabudana Vada were among the most popular choices. Mumbai and Bengaluru recorded strong demand for Sabudana Khichdi, with Pune and Jaipur also contributing to orders.

**Complete festive meal combinations also attracted consumers. Navratri Special Vrat Thalis, particularly those served with Singhara Poori, were among the preferred options.** Rajgira Poori and Aloo Hing three-course thalis also featured prominently, with Delhi, Bengaluru, Gurugram and Noida recording the highest demand.

**A customer in Noida placed an order worth Rs 11,072 on October 17-18, including 13 units of Navratri Special Vrat Thali with Singhara Poori, making it one of the largest fasting-food orders recorded during the weekend.**

**Traditional sweets also saw higher demand during the four-day festive period.** According to Swiggy, orders for traditional sweets increased by 36.4 percent between October 17 and October 20, 2026, compared with the corresponding festive period from September 29 to October 2, 2025.

**While metropolitan cities such as Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi and Hyderabad recorded substantial demand, several emerging markets, including Patna, Dehradun, Jodhpur, Gaya and Thiruvananthapuram, also reported strong sweet orders.** Among smaller cities and towns, Agartala, Shillong, Palwal and Bathinda recorded notable demand.

**A Mumbai customer placed an order worth Rs 9,870 for assorted traditional sweets and Coffee Rasgulla Tiramisu, marking the highest-value rasgulla-related order recorded by Swiggy between October 17 and October 20, 2026.**

Heritage Foods Limited has approved the amalgamation of its wholly owned subsidiary, Heritage Novandie Foods Limited, into the parent company. Heritage Novandie Foods operates the company's yogurt business under the Livo brand. ***The proposed merger is aimed at strengthening Heritage Foods' value-added dairy portfolio, simplifying its corporate structure and improving operational efficiency.***

The consolidation is expected to bring the subsidiary's business and financial resources closer to Heritage Foods' broader dairy operations. It is also intended to improve coordination across production, distribution, and brand development as the company expands its value-added dairy business. ***Heritage Foods is increasing its focus on value-added dairy products as part of its strategy to diversify revenue beyond liquid milk.*** Excluding ghee and butter, value-added products (VAP) accounted for 35.4 percent of dairy revenue in Q2 FY2026-27 and 39.6 percent in the first half of FY2026-27.

In the corresponding periods last year, the contribution stood at 31.3 percent and 33.7 percent, respectively. ***The company aims to increase the contribution of value-added products to approximately 50 percent over the next three years.*** The strategy is intended to build a more balanced revenue mix by increasing the share of branded and differentiated dairy products. Value-added dairy products can also help reduce the company's relative dependence on liquid milk, which is more exposed to seasonal demand changes and commodity price fluctuations.

The proposed amalgamation is expected to bring Livo's yogurt business into Heritage Foods' wider dairy platform. The company intends to align brand development more closely with its consumer reach, distribution network and production capabilities. ***The integration is also expected to simplify the group's corporate structure by eliminating a separate legal entity and reducing overlapping statutory, regulatory and administrative requirements.***

Heritage Foods expects the consolidation to support more coordinated management, faster decision-making and improved utilisation of financial and operational resources. The company also plans to streamline business processes and administrative costs through the integration.

> Brahmani Nara, Executive Director of Heritage Foods Limited said, “***Our focus remains on building a stronger, more integrated and future-ready dairy business. The proposed amalgamation of Heritage Novandie Foods is an important step in strengthening our value-added dairy platform, while simplifying the overall structure and enabling greater alignment across the business. As we continue to scale differentiated and branded dairy products, we believe this integration will further strengthen our platform for sustainable growth and enhance operational efficiency over the long term.***”

***The proposed amalgamation forms part of Heritage Foods' broader efforts to expand its value-added dairy portfolio, strengthen its branded product business and improve operational efficiency.*** The company is targeting a higher contribution from value-added products over the next three years as it works to diversify its dairy revenue mix.

Havells India reported an 11.1 percent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 353 crore in the second quarter of FY2026-27, while revenue rose 34.6 percent to Rs 6,417 crore. ***In the corresponding quarter last year, the electrical goods manufacturer recorded a net profit of Rs 317 crore and revenue of Rs 4,767 crore.***

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 30.5 percent to Rs 576 crore during the quarter. ***Profit before tax rose 15.1 percent to Rs 476 crore, compared with Rs 414 crore in the year-ago period.*** The results reflect growth across Havells India's electrical products portfolio, with cables, switchgears and consumer durables contributing to revenue during the September quarter.

Havells India's cables business recorded the highest revenue among its reported segments, rising 47.9 percent year on year to Rs 2,999 crore from Rs 2,028 crore. The switchgears business reported a 31.3 percent increase in revenue to Rs 782 crore. ***Revenue from electrical consumer durables grew 10.7 percent to Rs 1,072 crore, reflecting growth across the company's consumer electrical product categories.***

***The Lloyd business, which operates in the consumer durables segment, recorded a 28.4 percent increase in revenue to Rs 615 crore.*** Meanwhile, the lighting and fixtures business reported revenue of Rs 449 crore, up 7 percent year on year. The company's renewables business recorded the fastest growth among its reported segments, with revenue increasing 147.8 percent to Rs 329 crore from Rs 133 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue from other businesses also increased, rising 19.3 percent to Rs 171 crore during the quarter. ***The performance across these segments contributed to Havells India's overall revenue growth as demand continued across its electrical equipment and consumer products portfolio.***

Commenting on the company's performance, Chairman and Managing Director Anil Rai Gupta said demand remained steady despite inflationary pressures. He also expressed confidence in the ongoing festive season, while acknowledging continued macroeconomic uncertainties. The company's latest quarterly results come as consumer demand and festive-season sales remain important factors for India's electrical goods and consumer durables industry.

Havells India operates across several categories, including cables, switchgears, lighting, electrical consumer durables, renewables and air conditioning products under its Lloyd business. Its performance across these segments will remain relevant as the company navigates input cost pressures and changing consumer demand in the coming quarters.

Colgate-Palmolive (India) Limited reported net sales of Rs 1,692 crore in the second quarter of FY2026-27, marking a 12.2 percent year-on-year increase from Rs 1,507 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The oral care and personal care company recorded net profit of Rs 342 crore, compared with Rs 328 crore a year earlier. ***The results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, mark the second consecutive quarter of double-digit domestic sales growth for the company. Excluding one-off charges and exceptional items, net profit after tax increased 5.5 percent year on year.***

Colgate-Palmolive India's toothpaste portfolio recorded high-single-digit volume growth during the quarter, supported by its premium toothpaste range and Colgate MaxFresh. The company attributed its overall performance to growth across its brands and distribution channels.

> Manish Anandani, Managing Director and CEO of Colgate-Palmolive (India) Limited said, "***We are delighted to report double-digit topline growth for the second consecutive quarter. This consistent performance reflects broad-based growth momentum across our brands and distribution channels. The Toothpaste portfolio delivered high-single digit volume expansion, led by our Premium Toothpaste range and strong performance in Colgate MaxFresh. Driven by a consistent focus on the Funding the Growth program, gross margin expanded by 40 bps year-on-year to 69.6 percent in Q2. We remain committed to navigating commodity cost fluctuations through disciplined cost savings and calibrated pricing actions. Capitalising on this healthy and competitive margin profile, we further stepped up investments in brand building and premiumisation throughout the quarter. Looking ahead, we expect to deliver robust growth, anchored by a best-in-class science-backed product portfolio tailored across consumer benefits and reinforced by strategic advertising investments.***"

The company continued to invest in brand building, product innovation and premiumisation during the quarter. ***Its initiatives included expanding communication for Colgate Visible White and partnering with athletes for Colgate Total.*** The company also introduced themed oral care products, including a Harry Potter collection for children and adults and a Bluey-themed toothpaste featuring a vacuum-locked pump dispenser.

***In the third quarter, Colgate-Palmolive India partnered with television programme Kaun Banega Crorepati to promote night-time brushing habits. The initiative features Amitabh Bachchan delivering 100 unique sign-offs, one for each episode during the season.*** These activities form part of the company's efforts to increase consumer engagement and support demand across its oral care portfolio.

Colgate-Palmolive India's gross margin expanded by 40 basis points year on year to 69.6 percent in Q2 FY2026-27. The company attributed the improvement to its Funding the Growth programme. ***The company said it is addressing fluctuations in commodity costs through cost-saving measures and pricing adjustments while increasing spending on brand building and premium products.*** Its focus on premiumisation, distribution and product innovation is expected to support its growth plans in the coming quarters.

Alongside its quarterly results, the company's board declared a first interim dividend of Rs 24 per equity share of face value Rs 1 for FY2026-27. The total dividend payout will amount to Rs 653 crore. ***Payments are scheduled to begin on November 19, 2026, for shareholders whose names appear in the company's register of members or beneficial owners as of November 2, 2026.***

The quarterly results reflect continued growth in Colgate-Palmolive India's core oral care business, alongside higher investments in marketing and premium products. The company will look to sustain sales momentum while managing commodity cost fluctuations and supporting demand across its product portfolio.

Satiya Nutraceuticals Private Limited, acquired by Marico, has introduced Joyun, a skincare brand inspired by Korean beauty innovations and developed for Indian consumers. Operating on the philosophy of “seriously playful skincare,” **the brand combines science-backed formulations with distinctive textures and application formats to offer skincare products tailored to Indian skin needs.**

**Joyun is entering the market with 13 products across two ingredient-led ranges, Centella and Rose PDRN.** The ranges focus on skin-soothing, hydration, and rejuvenation, addressing consumer demand for skincare products that combine formulation efficacy with an engaging user experience.

**The launch comes amid growing interest in Korean beauty products in India, driven by ingredient-focused formulations, product innovation and the influence of Korean popular culture.** Joyun aims to establish its presence by combining internationally recognised skincare ingredients with products developed for Indian consumers.

**The brand’s formulations are dermatologist-tested, with an emphasis on safety, efficacy and compatibility with Indian skin.**

**The Rose PDRN range uses a rose-derived ingredient alongside other active ingredients.** PDRN, or Polydeoxyribonucleotide, is a DNA-derived compound associated with skin repair and regeneration. The range combines these ingredients with formulations designed to offer a sensory skincare experience in line with Joyun’s brand philosophy.

**The Centella range focuses on calming the skin, providing hydration and supporting the skin barrier.** It is positioned for consumers seeking products to address the effects of environmental exposure and everyday lifestyle-related stressors.

**Joyun’s broader concept, described as “The Lab of Play,” centres on making skincare both functional and enjoyable.** The brand incorporates lightweight textures and distinctive application formats to make daily skincare more engaging while maintaining its focus on science-backed formulations.

> **Rishubh Satiya, Founder, Satiya Nutraceuticals Pvt. Ltd. said,** *“At Satiya Nutraceuticals, we have always focused on building brands that address evolving consumer needs through innovation. Our ambition is to create a trusted brand that delivers visible results while making skincare a joyful everyday ritual.”*

**Backed by Marico, an established fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company in India, Satiya Nutraceuticals is focusing on products that combine safety, efficacy, and sensory appeal.** With Joyun, the company is entering the skincare segment with an offering that draws on Korean beauty trends while targeting the preferences and requirements of Indian consumers.

Omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone reported operating revenue of Rs 745 crore in the second quarter of FY2026-27, marking a 45 percent year-on-year increase from Rs 513.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. ***However, the company recorded a net loss of Rs 4.4 crore during the September quarter, compared with a net profit of Rs 6 crore in the preceding quarter.***

The latest loss was 92 percent lower than the Rs 52 crore loss reported in the year-ago period. ***Including other income of Rs 24.4 crore, BlueStone's total income stood at Rs 769 crore for the quarter.*** Total expenses increased 34 percent year on year to Rs 772 crore, driven by raw material costs, employee benefit expenses and other operating costs.

This represented an increase of 27 stores from the 352 outlets operating at the end of June.

The expansion forms part of BlueStone's strategy to combine online sales with a growing physical store network, giving customers access to its jewellery collections through multiple channels. ***BlueStone's customer base reached 10.24 lakh by the end of September, crossing the one-million mark during the quarter.*** Repeat customers accounted for 56.3 percent of revenue in Q2 FY2026-27, compared with 51.4 percent in the corresponding period last year.

***The increase in repeat customer contribution highlights the growing role of returning buyers in the company's sales mix.*** Despite higher operating revenue and a wider store network, BlueStone's quarterly results reflect the impact of rising expenses on its bottom line. ![Swiggy Q2 Loss Reaches Rs 922 Cr as Instamart Eyes Margin Gains](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/sjjdebbfb.jpg)

Swiggy reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 922 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 791 crore in the previous quarter. ***However, the loss narrowed from Rs 1,092 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, as revenue from operations increased 36 percent year-on-year to Rs 7,571 crore.***

The food delivery and quick commerce company is also preparing to transition Instamart to an inventory-led operating model after securing the necessary approvals to qualify as an Indian-owned and controlled company. ***The change is expected to give Instamart greater control over inventory, procurement, and pricing, with the potential to improve contribution margins.***

According to reports, the transition could improve Instamart's contribution margin by up to 80 basis points. ***The expected benefit comes as the quick commerce business continues to invest in customer acquisition, pricing, and expansion of its dark store network.*** Instamart's net order value (NOV) grew 31.4 percent year-on-year to Rs 6,954 crore in Q2 FY27, while the platform added 69 dark stores during the quarter. Its total network reached 1,240 stores across 133 cities as of September 30, 2026.

Despite the growth in order value, Instamart continued to report losses. ***Its adjusted EBITDA loss stood at Rs 895 crore in the September quarter, reflecting spending on pricing, marketing and network expansion.*** Swiggy expects the inventory-led model to improve control over sourcing, product assortment and supply chain operations. Direct inventory ownership may also help the company manage procurement costs and reduce wastage, although the effect on profitability will depend on operating efficiency and order growth.

***Swiggy's food delivery business recorded adjusted EBITDA of Rs 341 crore, its highest reported level, with a margin of 3.4 percent of gross order value (GOV).*** Food delivery GOV increased 17.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 10,054 crore. The company attributed the performance to improved delivery efficiency and higher advertising revenue. It is also expanding its affordable-meal offering through Toing, a separate platform designed to reach customers seeking lower-priced food options.

The food delivery business's profitability provides a source of earnings as Swiggy continues to invest in Instamart's expansion and works towards improving its unit economics. ***Swiggy's revenue from operations rose to Rs 7,571 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 5,561 crore in the year-ago period.*** Total expenses increased to Rs 8,703 crore from Rs 6,711 crore a year earlier.

The results highlight the difference in performance between Swiggy's two main businesses. ***Food delivery reported record adjusted EBITDA, while Instamart continued to incur losses as it expanded its quick commerce network.*** The planned inventory-led transition is expected to give Instamart greater flexibility in managing products and supply chains. The extent to which this change improves margins will depend on how effectively Swiggy converts its growing order volumes into sustainable profitability.

Sapphire Foods India, the operator of KFC and Pizza Hut restaurants in India and Sri Lanka, reported a net loss of Rs 1.1 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with a net profit of Rs 14.2 crore in the previous quarter. ***However, the company's losses narrowed from Rs 12.8 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.***

***Revenue from operations increased 19.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 888 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with Rs 742 crore a year earlier.*** Growth was supported by stronger sales at KFC and improving performance at Pizza Hut, according to the company's regulatory filing.

***Sapphire Foods' earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 23.5 percent year-on-year to Rs 126 crore from Rs 102 crore.*** Its EBITDA margin improved to 14.2 percent from 13.7 percent in the year-ago quarter.

KFC recorded 26 percent revenue growth during the September quarter, its strongest performance in the last 16 quarters. Same-store sales growth (SSSG) reached 14 percent, with dine-in and takeaway sales outperforming delivery. ***The business also recorded double-digit growth in transactions.***

***According to the company's investor presentation, value-focused offers supported customer acquisition and restaurant footfall.*** These included the Rs 99 Chicken Krisper Burger Meal, the Rs 149 Thalaiva Meal in Tamil Nadu and buy-one-get-one offers on chicken buckets. Marketing investments also supported sales during the quarter.

Pizza Hut recorded 7 percent revenue growth in the September quarter, alongside its highest same-store sales growth in seven quarters. Same-store transactions also grew at a double-digit rate. ***Value offers, including a Rs 99 four-course meal and buy-one-get-one deals, contributed to the improvement in sales.***

However, profitability remained a challenge for the business. Pizza Hut's EBITDA margin stood at negative 2.8 percent, down 100 basis points from the year-ago period, mainly due to higher energy costs. ***Sapphire Foods continued to add outlets during the quarter, opening 15 KFC restaurants and one Pizza Hut outlet in Sri Lanka. Its total restaurant network stood at 1,086 outlets as of September 30, 2026.***

The company's latest results reflect different performance trends across its two major restaurant brands. KFC recorded stronger revenue and same-store sales growth, while Pizza Hut showed an improvement in sales but continued to face pressure on operating margins.

Sapphire Foods operates KFC and Pizza Hut restaurants in India and Sri Lanka under franchise arrangements. Its performance comes amid continued competition in India's quick-service restaurant (QSR) market, where operators use value meals, promotional offers and marketing investments to attract customers while managing operating costs.

> Maanoj Tomar, Founder of AFC Furniture Solutions said, "***Pune is witnessing significant office expansion, particularly from GCCs and technology companies, who are also under pressure to make their spaces operational quickly. That’s where we come in, with a clear priority to strengthen execution, reduce installation timelines and develop furniture systems that grow with the business. We also see considerable potential in managed offices, where flexibility and cost efficiency are equally important.***"

The company is also targeting businesses in automotive technology, engineering and research and development (R&D). ***These sectors require office environments that support software development teams, product development functions and collaborative project work.*** AFC is prioritising managed office operators as businesses increasingly look for ready-to-occupy workspaces and flexible leasing arrangements. These operators require furniture systems that can be adapted for different tenants without extensive redesign or replacement.

***To address this demand, AFC is strengthening its relationships with workspace operators and commercial property developers.*** The company is also working to improve local project coordination, design consultancy partnerships and installation capabilities to manage large assignments across Pune's commercial districts.

> Tomar said, “***We strengthened our local project coordination, design consultancy relationships and installation capabilities to support large assignments across Pune's commercial corridors. The emphasis is on consistent quality, quicker turnaround and workplace solutions that optimise office investments for corporates.***”

AFC is drawing on its 4 lakh sq ft facility and national manufacturing capacity of 18,000 workstations and ergonomic seating systems per month to support corporate office projects. ***The company plans to use these manufacturing and execution capabilities to increase its participation in large corporate fit-outs and managed office projects in Pune.***

With GCC expansion and demand for flexible workspaces shaping the city's commercial property market, AFC is targeting a larger share of office furniture projects while strengthening its regional execution network in FY 2026-27.

Reliance Consumer Products Ltd (RCPL), the FMCG arm of Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), has entered India's ready-to-drink (RTD) dairy market by launching Joyland flavoured milk. The company has introduced the product in Tamil Nadu, offering strawberry and vanilla variants, as it expands its presence in the dairy and beverages segment. ***The launch comes about a month after RCPL announced its entry into India's ice cream market with Bombay Creamery.*** With Joyland, the company is adding packaged dairy beverages to its existing beverage portfolio.

> “***The launch extends RCPL’s total beverage portfolio, reinforcing its commitment to bringing world-class products to consumers at accessible prices,***” the company said in a statement.

RCPL Director T Krishnakumar said the company's entry into the ready-to-drink dairy category marks a step towards expanding its product range and offering consumers more choices.

> “***Tamil Nadu marks the beginning of this journey, as we build Joyland into a broader dairy beverages portfolio and progressively expand its reach across India,***” he said. Krishnakumar added that Joyland would be gradually introduced in other parts of the country.

India's ready-to-drink milk market is expanding as consumers increasingly seek convenient, hygienically packaged dairy products. Urbanisation and changing consumption patterns, particularly among younger buyers, are also contributing to demand for packaged milk-based beverages. ***The category includes flavoured milk and other value-added dairy drinks designed for convenient consumption outside the home.***

***According to market research firm IMARC Group, India's flavoured milk market was valued at around Rs 7,640 crore in 2025.*** The market is projected to reach Rs 38,550 crore by 2034, registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19.11 percent over the forecast period. This projected growth offers FMCG companies an opportunity to expand their presence in flavoured milk and other packaged dairy beverage categories.

RCPL has been expanding its product portfolio across consumer goods and beverages. The company, which was demerged from Reliance Retail and established as a direct subsidiary of RIL, reported revenue of Rs 8,600 crore in the June quarter of FY27. ***Reliance Industries has previously stated that it expects RCPL to reach Rs 1 lakh crore ($10.5 billion) in revenue over the next four years.***

The Joyland launch adds another category to RCPL's expansion strategy, with Tamil Nadu serving as the initial market before the company gradually extends distribution across India.

Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 125 crore for the September quarter, nearly double the Rs 65 crore recorded in the corresponding period last year. ***The growth came alongside a sharp increase in revenue from operations, reflecting higher business volumes across its food delivery and quick commerce segments.***

***According to the company's regulatory filing, revenue from operations rose to Rs 24,138 crore in the second quarter of the current financial year, compared with Rs 13,590 crore a year earlier.*** Total expenses also increased to Rs 24,166 crore from Rs 13,813 crore in the year-ago period. Blinkit added 308 net new stores during the quarter, taking its total store network to 2,751. The quick commerce platform expects to expand its network to more than 3,500 stores by March 2027.

Eternal reported continued growth in both its food delivery and quick commerce businesses. Zomato's food delivery net order value (NOV) increased 21.5 percent year-on-year to Rs 11,445 crore. Blinkit's quick commerce NOV grew 79.3 percent to Rs 20,940 crore. ***The platform also reported an adjusted EBITDA profit of Rs 184 crore, marking its sixth consecutive quarter of margin improvement.***

> Deepinder Goyal, Founder, Eternal said, "***We're happy with how the business is doing right now. That said, we try not to read too much into any single quarter. Our long-term expectation for food delivery has always been 20 per cent plus annual growth, and the last two quarters have brought us back to that range. This view didn't change last year when growth slowed, and it doesn't change now that it has picked up.***"

***Goyal's comments reaffirm the company's long-term expectation of annual food delivery growth above 20 percent, despite fluctuations in quarterly performance.*** Eternal plans to continue expanding Blinkit's quick commerce store network over the next two financial years. The company expects to exceed 3,500 stores by March 2027, with current plans pointing to approximately 5,000 stores by March 2028.

> Akshant Goyal, CFO, Eternal said, "***We now expect to cross 3,500 stores by March 2027, and our current plans point to about 5,000 stores by March 2028. Our cash balance and profits from both food delivery and quick commerce businesses, also let us fund this pace of growth comfortably. We expect adjusted EBITDA margins to keep improving through this expansion.***"

The planned expansion will increase Blinkit's physical store network as competition in India's quick commerce market continues. The company expects profitability and cash resources from its food delivery and quick commerce businesses to support the expansion while adjusted EBITDA margins improve.

PC Jewellers reported a 58 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 330.66 crore in the second quarter of FY27, supported by higher sales. ***The jewellery retailer also cleared its outstanding dues to all 14 consortium banks ahead of schedule, achieving debt-free status, according to its regulatory filing.***

YatriKart to Open 1,000 Quick Stop Stores Across India in Five Years

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![YatriKart to Open 1,000 Quick Stop Stores Across India in Five Years](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-21T174009.070.jpg)

YatriKart has partnered with MMG Group under a Rs 120 crore agreement to expand its convenience retail network in India, with plans to establish 1,000 Quick Stop stores over the next five years. The first phase will focus on 100 stores across Delhi NCR.

Under the Franchise Invested, Company Operated (FICO) model, MMG Group will fund store infrastructure and capital expenditure (CAPEX), while YatriKart will manage operating expenditure (OPEX), technology, supply chain, staffing and daily operations.

The partnership expands the relationship between the two companies, following MMG Group’s strategic equity investment in YatriKart in 2024. The latest agreement is aimed at building a technology-enabled convenience retail network across high-footfall locations in India.

## YatriKart Targets High-Footfall Retail Locations

YatriKart has started deploying Quick Stop stores across Delhi NCR as part of the initial phase. The company plans to prioritise locations such as fuel stations, highways, bus stands and other transit hubs before expanding into additional markets.

The company currently operates more than 80 stores across eight cities. Its outlets are located at petrol pumps, highways, hospitals, corporate parks, bus stands and transit hubs. The stores offer coffee, food, beverages and everyday essentials for consumers travelling or commuting.

YatriKart describes its business model as “Retail on the Go”, focusing on organised convenience retail at locations where consumers already spend time or travel through.

The company also plans to introduce a consumer app through which customers can locate stores along their routes and order products in advance. At participating fuel stations and other designated locations, customers will be able to receive orders directly from their vehicles.

## MMG Group Backs Nationwide Expansion

Gaurav Rana, Founder and CEO of YatriKart, said the partnership would support the company's plans to expand its convenience retail network.

“Quick commerce has transformed convenience at home. We believe there is a significant opportunity to make everyday essentials just as accessible outside the home.

Whether someone is commuting to work, refuelling, travelling or visiting a hospital, the need is often simple: a coffee, something to eat, a bottle of water or an essential they have forgotten. Our aim is to make YatriKart the familiar quick stop for these everyday moments.

This partnership is an important step towards building that network nationwide. Our focus is on making each store dependable for the customer and building an operating model that can scale through technology, a strong supply chain and consistent execution.”

Anant Agarwal, Promoter of MMG Group, said the investment was based on YatriKart’s operating experience and its work across different retail formats and locations.

“Quick commerce has transformed convenience at home. We believe the next big retail opportunity lies outside the home, serving millions of consumers who are constantly on the move.

Our confidence in YatriKart comes from its five years of experience on the ground. The team has worked across Indian Railways, Delhi Metro, hotels, hospitals and temples, and built a partner network of around 500 stores. That journey has given it valuable experience in distribution, supply chain and customer needs across different locations.

Through multiple pivots, YatriKart has refined its model, made difficult decisions to discontinue initiatives that did not work, and focused on the formats with stronger potential to scale. Along the way, it has built its technology backbone and established corporate partnerships that provide a potential location pool of around 60,000 sites.

We are backing both the market opportunity and a team that has learned, adapted and built the foundations for growth. That combination of experience, technology and access to locations is what gives us conviction in YatriKart’s ability to build a nationwide convenience retail network.”

Secret Alchemist, a clean fragrance brand co-founded by Samantha Ruth Prabhu, Ankita Thadani and Akash Valia, has crossed Rs 120 crore in revenue after recording 8x growth over eight months. The company has introduced a new 50ml Signature Size for its existing Signature perfume collection, priced at Rs 1,999, as it looks to expand its presence in India's fragrance market.

The new format, introduced in Mumbai on October 21, 2026, is positioned between trial-sized fragrances and full-sized bottles. The move comes as consumer preferences in India evolve, with fragrance users increasingly exploring multiple scents for different occasions and parts of the day.

The company said the new format is intended to make its Signature collection accessible to a wider consumer base while retaining its focus on clean formulations and ingredients sourced from India.

The Signature collection features fragrances formulated with an essential oil concentration of 25 percent or more. According to the company, the products are designed to offer longer-lasting scents and are free from parabens and phthalates. The brand also states that its fragrances are IFRA-certified, with ingredient and allergen information disclosed to consumers.

The collection includes Indian botanical ingredients such as vetiver, patchouli, saffron and tuberose. Secret Alchemist said these ingredients reflect its focus on incorporating Indian fragrance heritage and botanicals into its product range.

The introduction of the 50ml format comes as the Indian fragrance market sees growing interest in premium perfumes and consumers experiment with different fragrance profiles. The trend, often described as fragrance wardrobing, involves using different perfumes according to personal preferences, occasions and daily routines.

Secret Alchemist has a 35-year legacy in aromatherapy and wellness and has focused on clean fragrances since 2022. The company entered the perfumery segment in 2025, making fragrance a key part of its business strategy.

According to the brand, its shift towards perfumery has contributed to its recent growth, taking the business to Rs 120 crore in revenue after an 8x increase over eight months.

Commenting on the milestone, Akash Valia, Co-founder of Secret Alchemist, said, "Crossing ₹120 crore in eight months tells us Indian consumers are ready for clean fragrance at scale. Scaling the Signature collection in a new format is the next step, celebrating a luxury range made with rare Indian ingredients from homegrown plantations, at a price that makes premium clean perfume accessible. Next, we want to take this into new product categories, new geographies and a much stronger offline presence,"

Ankita Thadani, Co-founder of Secret Alchemist, said, "We didn't set out to build just another perfume brand. We set out to build one consumers could trust with something they put on their skin every day. The Signature collection takes that promise into luxury. Vetiver, patchouli, saffron and tuberose are some of India's most precious ingredients, and we wanted to celebrate them in their purest, cleanest form,"

> Samantha Ruth Prabhu, Co-founder of Secret Alchemist, said, “Crossing ₹120 crore is a proud moment for all of us. More than anything, it tells us that what we’re building at Secret Alchemist is connecting with people, and that means a lot. We’ve always believed that India has the ingredients, heritage and creativity to build a fragrance brand that can stand alongside the best in the world, without compromising on our clean philosophy. The Signature collection has continued to evolve, and I’m excited for more people to experience its newest expression,"

Secret Alchemist sells its products through its direct-to-consumer platform and online marketplaces, including Amazon, Nykaa and Flipkart. Its distribution network also includes quick-commerce platforms Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart, alongside offline retail stores.

The company plans to expand into additional product categories and geographies while strengthening its offline presence. The introduction of the new Signature Size forms part of its efforts to broaden access to its premium fragrance portfolio and build its position in India's beauty and personal care market.

Founded by Ankita Thadani and Akash Valia, Secret Alchemist added actor Samantha Ruth Prabhu as a co-founder in 2024. The brand's latest revenue milestone and product introduction reflect its focus on growing its fragrance business across digital and physical retail channels.

IVS Group has appointed Atish Bhatia as Group Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) and Head of IVS Fashion, strengthening its leadership as it looks to expand its presence in India's fashion and consumer brands market.

In his dual role, Bhatia will oversee the group's marketing strategy, brand development and communications while leading the business strategy and expansion of its fashion portfolio, which includes The BT Club and NotreDeim.

The BT Club is a streetwear brand targeting Gen Z consumers, while NotreDeim operates in the premium lifestyle apparel segment. Bhatia will focus on developing the brands, strengthening their market positioning and driving growth in India's evolving apparel market.

Bhatia brings more than a decade of experience across fintech, media, digital platforms, brand partnerships, monetisation and growth strategy. Before joining IVS Group, he served as Chief Marketing Officer at FiatPe, where he led marketing initiatives focused on brand building, merchant engagement and business growth in India's digital payments sector.

He previously worked as Head of Sponsorship at Saregama India Ltd., overseeing strategic partnerships and brand alliances. At Condé Nast India, he worked on revenue models and digital monetisation across premium media platforms.

His earlier experience includes working as Monetisation Manager for Dice Media at Pocket Aces and as Region Head for West and South at ELLE India, where he managed digital, print, brand solutions and experiential initiatives.

Bhatia has also held roles at Times Internet, Forbes India, Naukri.com and Hindustan Times, contributing to business expansion and revenue growth across media and digital businesses.

IVS Fashion is the digital-first consumer brand portfolio of IVS Group. Its brands cater to different consumer segments, with The BT Club focusing on Gen Z-oriented streetwear and NotreDeim targeting the premium lifestyle apparel market.

Through the appointment, IVS Group aims to strengthen its group-wide brand strategy while developing its fashion business. Bhatia's responsibilities will include driving brand growth, expanding the portfolio's market presence and building consumer relevance for both labels.

IVS Group operates as a founder-led business platform with independently operating companies across sectors including technology, infrastructure, manufacturing, education and consumer brands.

The appointment places marketing and fashion business leadership under Bhatia as the group looks to develop its consumer-facing businesses and expand its presence in India's apparel market.

The inauguration marks a step in the organisation's global expansion and brings its gemological testing services to Surat, a major centre for diamond processing and the gems and jewellery trade in India.

The laboratory will offer services to determine whether diamonds are natural or synthetic. According to the organisation, the facility will follow the reporting standards and professional practices adopted across the ICA | GemLab group.

Surat is a major global centre for diamond processing, with an established network of manufacturers, traders and other businesses operating across the diamond value chain. The city's position in the industry makes it a strategic location for gemological testing services.

ICA | GemLab India said, “Surat is the world’s largest centre for diamond policing, making it an important location for our laboratory. With the new facility, ICA | GemLab aims to establish a direct presence in India's gems and jewellery market and improve access to gemological testing and reporting for businesses across the sector.

JK Maxx Paints has entered the sustainable paints segment with the introduction of JK Naturals, a new paints brand, and JK Naturals Aura, its first product. The company, a subsidiary of JK Cement Ltd., is positioning the range in India's decorative paints market, combining recycled and bio-based materials with interior paint technology.

Introduced as a nature-focused paint, JK Naturals Aura Luxury Interior Emulsion contains more than 40 percent eco-friendly content, including over 10 percent bio-based emulsion. According to the company, the product also incorporates air-purification technology designed to reduce formaldehyde in indoor environments and help improve indoor air quality.

The launch adds to JK Maxx Paints' portfolio as paint manufacturers explore sustainability-led formulations and materials for the home improvement and interior decoration market.

JK Maxx Paints has developed JK Naturals Aura in collaboration with Shark Solutions, a Denmark-based cleantech company specialising in recycling. The product incorporates recycled polyvinyl butyral (PVB) recovered from end-of-life laminated glass.

The use of recycled PVB converts post-consumer waste into a raw material for paint manufacturing, supporting the reuse of materials within the production cycle. The company has also incorporated recycled packaging as part of the product's sustainability approach.

The luxury interior emulsion is available in more than 2,000 shades and features a sheen finish and smooth texture. Its combination of recycled and bio-based inputs is intended to address consumer interest in home improvement products with a focus on environmental considerations.

The company plans to introduce JK Naturals Aura in phases, beginning in North India between late October and mid-November 2026. A nationwide rollout is planned subsequently.

> Commenting on the launch, Nitish Chopra, Business Head, White Cement and Paints, JK Maxx Paints, said, “At JK Maxx Paints, we have always focused on developing solutions that respond to the evolving needs of consumers. With JK Naturals, we are taking this commitment forward by bringing sustainability into the home beautification category. Our first product, JK Naturals Aura brings together innovative materials, air-purification technology and a premium finish, offering consumers a thoughtful choice for their homes. Our collaboration with Shark Solutions further reflects our endeavour to explore innovative materials and create products that balance performance with environmental responsibility.”

Alongside the product introduction, JK Maxx Paints is rolling out a 'Pledge a Tree' initiative through a QR code printed on the packaging. Consumers can scan the code and take an online pledge, following which the company will plant a tree for each pledge taken online.

According to the company, the initiative is intended to encourage consumer participation in tree plantation and environmental conservation. The launch will also be supported by a digital film outlining the brand's approach to sustainable home beautification.

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)

![Myntra Reports Rs 5,242 Cr Revenue in FY26 as Ad Income Rises 35 Pc](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/swednfnem.jpg)

Myntra Designs Private Limited, which operates the Myntra fashion and lifestyle platform and is part of the Flipkart Group, reported revenue from operations of Rs 5,242.5 crore in FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). ***Excluding logistics and shipping services, Myntra's revenue from operations increased 12 percent to Rs 4,123.3 crore from Rs 3,673.3 crore in FY25.*** The growth was supported by higher revenue from advertising and marketplace services.

Revenue from advertising services rose 35.2 percent to Rs 1,236.4 crore from Rs 914.5 crore. ***Revenue from marketplace and collection services increased 3 percent to Rs 2,657.3 crore from Rs 2,580.2 crore, while other operating revenue grew 28.6 percent to Rs 229.6 crore.***

Revenue from logistics and shipping services declined to Rs 1,119.2 crore from Rs 2,390.5 crore in FY25. ***This reduction contributed to the fall in total revenue from operations compared with Rs 6,063.8 crore in the previous financial year.*** Myntra's total expenses increased 0.6 percent to Rs 5,757.7 crore from Rs 5,726 crore in FY25. Direct expenses, including logistics charges, fell 14 percent to Rs 1,841 crore. Other expenses, which include advertising and business promotion, rose 12.8 percent to Rs 3,059.8 crore, while employee benefit expenses increased 3.7 percent to Rs 776.9 crore.

The company reported a loss before tax of Rs 441.9 crore in FY26, compared with a profit before tax of Rs 411 crore in FY25. The previous year's profit included a deferred tax credit. ***The Myntra financial statements are standalone figures. The company is also included in the consolidated financial statements of its holding company, Flipkart Internet Private Limited.***

Flipkart Group comprises Flipkart, Myntra and Cleartrip, along with platform services, logistics and other specialised businesses. In a statement, the group said FY26 was the first financial year in which consolidated group figures were reflected in Flipkart Internet Private Limited following its redomiciliation to India.

***The group said its businesses operate through multiple legal entities and share technology infrastructure, loyalty programmes and supply chain capabilities.*** It advised stakeholders to refer to the consolidated financial statements of Flipkart Internet Private Limited when assessing the group's overall performance.

On a consolidated basis, Flipkart Group's revenue grew 18 percent in FY26. Its revenue from operations reached Rs 1,45,880 crore, compared with a restated Rs 1,23,451 crore in FY25. The group's consolidated loss for the year stood at Rs 8,468 crore, against a restated loss of Rs 8,646 crore in the previous financial year.

Myntra said customer growth has reached about 30 percent so far in FY27, which began in April 2026. The company also said it is on track to reach 100 million monthly active users during the ongoing festive season. ***Its flagship Big Fashion Festival (BFF), which began on October 8, recorded a fourfold increase in demand over business-as-usual (BAU) levels during its first 24 hours, according to the company.***

Customers from Tier ll and Tier lll cities accounted for more than half of the orders placed on the first day. Jaipur, Lucknow, Patna, Indore, Ludhiana, Surat, Dehradun, Bhubaneswar and Mysuru were among the cities reporting high demand. ***Ahead of Durga Puja, Myntra reported demand from eastern India at seven times its business-as-usual level, led by West Bengal, Assam and Bihar.*** New customers from these regions increased 1.8 times over BAU levels, the company said.

Ethnic wear, casual wear, beauty essentials and sportswear were among the categories driving demand during the period. Flipkart Group clarified that the FY26 financial results provide a historical view of the business and should not be treated as a current trading update.

Uniqlo India reported a 44 percent year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 1,724 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, while net profit rose 41 percent to Rs 253 crore, according to filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). ***The Japanese apparel retailer, which entered the Indian market seven years ago, has more than quadrupled its revenue since FY22.*** The company currently operates more than 20 stores in India and plans to expand its retail network across the country.

***In its regulatory filing, Uniqlo India highlighted the country's long-term growth potential and outlined plans to open additional stores in existing markets as well as locations where it has yet to establish a presence.*** The company also plans to strengthen customer engagement through its mobile application and e-commerce operations.

Uniqlo's FY26 performance comes amid mixed results among established apparel retailers in India. ***Zara, which operates in the country through a joint venture between Spain's Inditex and Tata Group's Trent, reported a 1.2 percent decline in revenue to Rs 2,749 crore.*** Meanwhile, Shoppers Stop recorded 9 percent revenue growth to Rs 5,043 crore, while Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail reported an 11 percent increase to Rs 8,177 crore.

Uniqlo India's growth also reflects its parent company, Fast Retailing's, broader expansion priorities. In its global annual report, the group said Southeast Asia, India and Australia had recorded double-digit revenue growth for four consecutive years since FY22, identifying these markets as important areas for further expansion.

Fast Retailing aims to achieve annual sales of ¥100 billion, equivalent to around US$633 million, in each of these markets. ***To support this target, the group plans to strengthen local management teams and adapt its product assortment, marketing, store formats and e-commerce operations to suit tropical climates and regional consumer needs.***

The company's latest results underline India's growing importance to Uniqlo's international business. Its planned store expansion and investment in digital channels are expected to remain central to its efforts to increase its presence in the Indian apparel market.

![Burma Burma Operator Hunger Pangs Files DRHP for Rs 150 Cr IPO](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20%2813%29.jpg)

Hunger Pangs Limited, the operator of premium Burmese restaurant chain Burma Burma, has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO).

The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.79 crore equity shares by existing shareholders. The equity shares have a face value of Rs 2 each.

The OFS includes shares offered by promoters Ankit Virendra Gupta and Chirag Narendra Chhajer, along with other promoter group entities, institutional investors and individual shareholders. 

The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to establish new Burma Burma restaurants across India and for general corporate purposes. 

Panthomath Capital Advisors Private Limited is the sole book-running lead manager for the issue.

## **22 Restaurants Across Nine Cities**

Hunger Pangs has developed its restaurant business around Burmese cuisine, with an emphasis on cultural influences, menu research and experiential dining. The company follows standardised recipes, standard operating procedures, centralised procurement and structured employee training to maintain consistency across its outlets.

As of July 31, 2026, the company operated 22 restaurants, one delivery kitchen and three warehouses across nine Indian cities. Its outlets are located in premium malls, high streets and corporate parks. As of June 30, 2026, it had 21 restaurants with a combined seating capacity of 1,991 seats.

The company reported an average bill value of Rs 2,400 in the financial year 2025-26 (FY26).

## **Revenue Rises 46.56 Percent in FY26**

Hunger Pangs reported revenue from operations of Rs 1,554.97 million in FY26, up from Rs 1,060.99 million in FY25, marking a year-on-year increase of 46.56 percent.

Its EBITDA rose from Rs 213.54 million in FY25 to Rs 256.77 million in FY26. The EBITDA margin stood at 16.51 percent in FY26.

The company plans to expand its restaurant network, introduce new brands and cuisines, and continue investing in menu development. Its expansion strategy considers factors such as customer demand, location accessibility, property costs, consumption potential and suitability for the brand.

Beyond dine-in services, Hunger Pangs is developing its delivery and direct-to-consumer business. Delivery contributed 10.76 percent of revenue from operations in FY26. The company also operates Burma Burma Shop and is exploring ready-to-eat and packaged food products.

## **Dining Market Offers Growth Opportunity**

According to the F&S Report cited in the DRHP, India's full-service dining market was valued at approximately Rs 1.52 trillion in FY26 and is projected to reach Rs 2.18 trillion by FY30, growing at a compound annual growth rate of around 9.4 percent.

Rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and changing dining preferences are expected to support market growth. Demand for differentiated cuisines and dining experiences could also create opportunities for organised restaurant chains to expand across Indian cities.

![Cumin Co Launches New Pressure Cooker in India, Expands Kitchenware Portfolio](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/seoo%20imageee%20%286%29.jpg)

Cumin Co., a premium kitchenware brand, has entered India’s Rs 6,600-crore pressure cooker market with a new product featuring patented three-mode cooking technology, tri-ply stainless steel construction and a multi-layer safety system. The launch marks the brand’s expansion into a widely used kitchen category, with a focus on improving functionality, safety and ease of use.

The pressure cooker features MaestroValve, a patented pressure-control technology that combines three cooking modes in a single dial. The Steam mode is designed for vegetables, momos and dhokla; Cook mode caters to everyday staples such as dal, rice and pulao; and Express mode is intended for dishes such as rajma, chole and meat. According to the brand, the Express mode can enable cooking up to 30% faster.

> “The pressure cooker is indispensable to Indian cooking, yet consumers have largely learnt to work around its limitations rather than expect more from it. We see an opportunity to move the category beyond price and capacity towards a better cooking experience, driven by thoughtful engineering, better materials and meaningful functionality,” said Niharika Joshi, Co-founder, Cumin Co.

The cooker features a tri-ply construction made from 18/8 food-grade surgical stainless steel, designed to distribute heat evenly and accommodate different cooking requirements, including preparations involving acidic ingredients. It is compatible with all cooktops.

Safety features include a three-layer pressure-release system comprising a regulator, safety valve and gasket-release pathway. The product also comes with vertical steam release, a caged valve designed to help prevent foam and debris from obstructing the steam pathway, pressure and lid-lock indicators, and handles designed to remain cool to the touch.

Other features include minimum and maximum fill markings, a removable gasket that can be replaced without tools, and a common lid compatible with the 3.5-litre and 5.5-litre models. The product comes with a five-year warranty.

> Explaining the product development approach, Udit Lekhi, Co-founder, Cumin Co., said, “We approached the pressure cooker as an engineering challenge, rethinking how it distributes heat, adapts to different cooking needs and communicates pressure and readiness. With MaestroValve™ bringing three cooking modes into a single intuitive control, alongside tri-ply stainless steel construction and a multi-layer safety system, every design decision was driven by a practical need.”

He added that the aim was to improve the everyday cooking experience without adding complexity or requiring consumers to change their existing habits.

The launch extends Cumin Co.’s focus on material-conscious kitchenware into the pressure cooker category, where the brand is seeking to combine functional engineering with contemporary design. Its existing portfolio includes enameled cast iron cookware, kitchen tools and preparation essentials.

The new pressure cooker will initially be available through the brand’s direct-to-consumer website, followed by a phased expansion across online marketplaces and offline retail. The company has yet to announce the product’s pricing and purchase details.

With the launch, Cumin Co. is looking to build on its presence in the kitchenware market by introducing product-led innovation into an established category and addressing changing consumer expectations around materials, functionality and design.
